fields.doc: Metastore hosting the MCP service.

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
Resource name of the MCP service. Format:
`mcp-services/{catalog}.{schema}.{mcp_service}`. Each `{...}` component
is capped at 255 characters individually. Server-derived on Create from
`parent` + `mcp_service_id`; required and immutable on Update/Get/Delete.

fields.name: update_time
fields.doc: Time the MCP service was last modified.

fields.name: updated_by
fields.doc: Identity of the last updater.

types.name: McpServiceConfig
types.doc:
Operational configuration for an MCP service. Groups the source reference,
tool selectors, and rate limits -- the fields that configure how the MCP
service behaves at invocation time.

fields.name: include_tool_selectors
fields.doc:
Tool names or prefix patterns to expose from the MCP server. Use exact
tool names or prefix patterns such as `read_*`. An empty list exposes all
tools. At most 1,024 selectors are allowed, and each selector can contain
at most 256 characters.

fields.name: rate_limits
fields.doc:
Rate limits for tool invocations. Supported scopes are user, group,
service principal, the service as a whole, and each user by default.
Request and token limits are supported. Empty when no rate limit is
configured.

fields.name: source_connection
fields.doc: Unity Catalog connection referencing the MCP server. Required on Create.

types.name: McpServiceConfigSourceConnection
types.doc:
Unity Catalog connection that points to the MCP server. On Create, provide
`name` in the schema-scoped form
`connections/{catalog}.{schema}.{connection}`. On read, the service populates
the resolved connection metadata. If the connection is deleted, its reference
remains visible so you can identify the broken dependency.

fields.name: is_deleted
fields.doc:
Whether the referenced connection has been deleted. The MCP service keeps
the reference so callers can identify the broken dependency; tool
invocation fails until the source connection is updated.

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
Resource name of the Unity Catalog connection used to access the MCP
server, in the form `connections/{catalog}.{schema}.{connection}`.

fields.name: options
fields.doc:
Options needed to build the U2M authorize request, returned as a flat
map. When set, it includes: `authorization_endpoint` (OAuth authorize
URL), `token_endpoint` (token-exchange URL), `oauth_scope`
(space-separated scopes to request), `client_id` (OAuth client id), and
`oauth_provider` (the OAuth provider).

types.name: McpServiceUserMappedCredential
types.doc: A caller's per-user OAuth credential for an MCP service.

fields.name: options
fields.doc:
Token-expiry info for the credential, returned as a flat map:
`access_token_expiration` (always set) and `refresh_token_expiration`
(set when the credential has a refresh token). Both values are
timestamps.

fields.name: provisioning_info
fields.doc:
Provisioning state of the credential. `ACTIVE` means the caller is logged
in and the credential is usable; any other state means the login has not
completed.

types.name: McpServiceUserMappedCredentialLogin
types.doc:
Login input for an MCP service user credential. Carries the OAuth exchange
fields as a flat map.

fields.name: options
fields.doc:
OAuth exchange fields: `pkce_verifier`, `authorization_code`, and
`oauth_redirect_uri`.

fields.name: storage_root
fields.doc: The storage root URL for metastore

fields.name: storage_root_credential_id
fields.doc: UUID of storage credential to access the metastore storage_root.

fields.name: storage_root_credential_name
fields.doc: Name of the storage credential to access the metastore storage_root.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.doc: Time at which the metastore was last modified, in epoch milliseconds.

fields.name: updated_by
fields.doc: Username of user who last modified the metastore.

types.name: ModelProviderService
types.doc:
A Unity Catalog securable that stores authentication and request
configuration for an external model provider, such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI,
or Amazon Bedrock. Model service destinations reference it to send requests
to that provider.

A model provider service can be referenced by multiple model services. A
model service can route across multiple model provider services for traffic
splitting or failover.

fields.name: comment
fields.doc: User-provided description.

fields.name: config
fields.doc:
Provider authentication, exposed models, request-forwarding controls,
rate limits, and payload logging. Required on Create. On Update, it is
required only when `config` or one of its subpaths appears in
`update_mask`.

fields.name: create_time
fields.doc: Time the provider service was created.

fields.name: created_by
fields.doc: Creator identity.

fields.name: effective_owner
fields.doc: Owner of the model provider service.

fields.name: etag
fields.doc:
Optimistic concurrency token returned on every read. To make an Update or
Delete conditional, pass the last-read value in that request's `etag`
field. In REST responses, this value is a base64 string; URL-encode it
when setting the `etag` query parameter.

fields.name: metastore_id
fields.doc: Metastore hosting the provider service.

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
Resource name of the provider service. Format:
`model-provider-services/{catalog}.{schema}.{model_provider_service}`.
Each `{...}` component is capped at 255 characters individually.
Server-derived on Create from `parent` + `model_provider_service_id`;
required and immutable on Update/Get/Delete.

fields.name: update_time
fields.doc: Time the provider service was last modified.

fields.name: updated_by
fields.doc: Identity of the last updater.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfig
types.doc:
Behavioral configuration for a ModelProviderService: provider authentication
and provider-specific fields, the catalog of models this provider service can
route to, and the passthrough policy that governs how request headers, query
parameters, and unmanaged subpaths cross the trust boundary to the upstream
provider.

fields.name: allow_all_targets
fields.doc:
When true, accepts any model exposed by the upstream provider; `targets`
is not required and does not restrict routability. When false, only
models listed in `targets` are routable. Defaults to false.

fields.name: forward_headers
fields.doc:
Whether to forward incoming HTTP headers to the upstream provider.
Defaults to false and is configured for the entire provider service, not
per request. Upstream authentication is configured separately in the
provider-specific configuration.

fields.name: forward_query_parameters
fields.doc:
Whether to forward incoming query parameters to the upstream provider.
Defaults to false and is configured for the entire provider service, not
per request.

fields.name: forward_unmanaged_paths
fields.doc:
Whether to proxy paths that AI Gateway does not recognize as configured
provider-native API types. Defaults to false. When true, these paths are
forwarded unchanged to the upstream provider. When false, only recognized
API paths are served. Enabling this broadens the upstream API surface
exposed through the provider service.

fields.name: inference_table
fields.doc:
Payload logging configuration for requests sent directly to this provider
service. Requests routed through a model service are captured by that
model service's inference table instead.

fields.name: provider_type
fields.doc:
External model provider. Required on Create and immutable thereafter. Set
the matching provider-specific configuration, such as `openai`,
`azure_openai`, or `amazon_bedrock`.

fields.name: rate_limits
fields.doc:
Rate limits for requests sent directly to this provider service. Requests
routed through a model service use that model service's rate limits
instead.

fields.name: targets
fields.doc:
Models and provider-native API types exposed by this provider service.
Each entry must include at least one `native_api_types` value. When
`allow_all_targets` is false, at least one entry is required and model
service destinations can reference only listed models. When
`allow_all_targets` is true, any upstream model is routable; entries in
this list provide API-type metadata without restricting other models.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigAmazonBedrockProviderConfig
types.doc: Amazon Bedrock provider configuration.

fields.name: direct
fields.doc: Amazon Bedrock region and authentication configuration.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigAmazonBedrockProviderDirectConfig
types.doc:
Direct form of Amazon Bedrock provider config.

Authentication is one of two mutually exclusive modes, exactly one of which
must be supplied on Create: - Access keys: set `aws_access_key`, leave
`service_credential` unset. - Unity Catalog service credential: set
`service_credential.name` to the resource name `credentials/{name}`, leave
`aws_access_key` unset. The credential value lives in Unity Catalog and is
referenced by name, not held on this message. Setting more than one mode is
rejected.

fields.name: aws_access_key
fields.doc:
AWS access-key-pair authentication. Set `access_key_id` and
`secret_access_key.plaintext`. Mutually exclusive with
`service_credential`.

fields.name: region
fields.doc:
AWS region where the Bedrock endpoint is hosted (e.g., `us-east-1`).
Required on Create.

fields.name: service_credential
fields.doc:
Reference to a Unity Catalog service credential authorizing Bedrock
requests. On Create, supply `service_credential.name` in the form
`credentials/{name}`. Required on Create when using service-credential
authentication; mutually exclusive with `aws_access_key`. The credential
is referenced by name; its value is not carried here. Only supported on
AWS-hosted workspaces.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigAnthropicProviderConfig
types.doc:
Anthropic provider configuration. Exactly one of `direct` or `relayed` must
be set on Create; the two are mutually exclusive.

fields.name: direct
fields.doc:
Direct authentication with an API key supplied in
`direct.api_key.plaintext`. Required unless `relayed` is set.

fields.name: relayed
fields.doc:
Relayed authentication. Each inference request supplies the caller's
OAuth token, which is forwarded to Anthropic. No Anthropic credential is
stored. Mutually exclusive with `direct`.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigAnthropicProviderDirectConfig
types.doc: Direct form of Anthropic provider config.

fields.name: api_key
fields.doc:
Anthropic API key. Required when creating the service. Supply the value
in `api_key.plaintext`.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigAnthropicProviderRelayedConfig
types.doc:
Relayed Anthropic provider configuration. Each inference request supplies the
caller's OAuth token, which is forwarded to Anthropic. No Anthropic
credential is stored.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigAwsAccessKey
types.doc: AWS access-key-pair auth for Amazon Bedrock: a SigV4-signing key pair.

fields.name: access_key_id
fields.doc:
AWS access key ID. Required on Create when using access-key auth. Treated
as username-equivalent (not a secret value): round-trips on reads and is
scrubbed from audit logs.

fields.name: secret_access_key
fields.doc:
AWS secret access key paired with `access_key_id`. Required when creating
a service with access-key authentication. Supply the value in
`secret_access_key.plaintext`.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigAzureOpenAiProviderConfig
types.doc: Azure OpenAI provider configuration.

fields.name: direct
fields.doc: Azure OpenAI endpoint and authentication configuration.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigAzureOpenAiProviderDirectConfig
types.doc:
Direct form of Azure OpenAI provider config. Exactly one of three
mutually-exclusive auth modes must be supplied on Create: - API key: set
`api_key`, leave `entra_service_principal` and `service_credential` unset. -
Entra ID (service principal): set `entra_service_principal`, leave `api_key`
and `service_credential` unset. - Unity Catalog service credential: set
`service_credential.name` to the resource name `credentials/{name}`, leave
`api_key` and `entra_service_principal` unset. The credential value lives in
Unity Catalog and is referenced by name, not held on this message. Only
supported on Azure-hosted workspaces. Setting more than one mode is rejected.

fields.name: api_key
fields.doc:
Azure OpenAI API key. Supply the value in `api_key.plaintext`. Mutually
exclusive with Entra ID and Unity Catalog service credential
authentication.

fields.name: base_url
fields.doc:
Full Azure OpenAI endpoint base URL, e.g.
`https://myresource.openai.azure.com`. Required on Create.

fields.name: entra_service_principal
fields.doc:
Entra ID service-principal authentication. Set `tenant_id`, `client_id`,
and `client_secret.plaintext`. Mutually exclusive with `api_key` and
`service_credential`.

fields.name: service_credential
fields.doc:
Reference to a Unity Catalog service credential authorizing Azure OpenAI
requests. On Create, supply `service_credential.name` in the form
`credentials/{name}`. Required on Create when using service-credential
authentication; mutually exclusive with `api_key` and
`entra_service_principal`. The credential is referenced by name; its
value is not carried here. Only supported on Azure-hosted workspaces.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigCustomProviderApiKeyHeaderAuth
types.doc:
Header-based API-key authentication for a custom provider: the secret is
forwarded on outbound requests under a caller-chosen HTTP header, as
`<api_key_name>: <api_key_value>`.

fields.name: api_key_name
fields.doc:
HTTP header name that carries the API key on outbound requests (e.g.,
`Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key`). The value forwarded under this header is
supplied via `api_key_value`.

fields.name: api_key_value
fields.doc:
Secret value forwarded under the `api_key_name` header on outbound
requests. Supplied as inline plaintext via `ProviderSecret.plaintext`.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigCustomProviderConfig
types.doc:
Custom OpenAI-compatible provider configuration with bearer-token
authentication.

fields.name: direct
fields.doc: Endpoint and authentication configuration for the custom provider.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigCustomProviderDirectConfig
types.doc:
Direct form of a custom provider configuration. Set `api_key` to send the
secret as an `Authorization` bearer token, or `header_auth` to forward it
under a caller-chosen HTTP header.

fields.name: api_key
fields.doc:
Bearer token forwarded in the `Authorization` header. Supply the value in
`api_key.plaintext`.

fields.name: base_url
fields.doc:
Endpoint URL of the OpenAI-compatible service (e.g.,
`https://api.example.com/v1`). Required on Create.

fields.name: header_auth
fields.doc:
Header-based API-key auth: the secret is forwarded on outbound requests
under a caller-chosen HTTP header rather than as an `Authorization`
bearer token. Set this instead of `api_key` for header auth.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigEntraServicePrincipal
types.doc:
Entra ID (Azure AD) service-principal authentication. The `tenant_id` and
`client_id` identify the service principal, and `client_secret` authenticates
it. AI Gateway exchanges these credentials for an Entra bearer token for
requests to Azure OpenAI or Microsoft Foundry.

fields.name: client_id
fields.doc: Entra ID client (application) ID. Required on Create.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.doc: Entra ID client secret. Supply the value in `client_secret.plaintext`.

fields.name: tenant_id
fields.doc: Entra ID (Azure AD) tenant ID. Required on Create.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigExternalModelProviderType
types.doc: External LLM provider for an EXTERNAL_FOUNDATION_MODEL destination.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigGeminiEnterpriseProviderConfig
types.doc: Gemini Enterprise provider configuration.

fields.name: direct
fields.doc: Gemini Enterprise project, region, and authentication configuration.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigGeminiEnterpriseProviderDirectConfig
types.doc:
Direct Gemini Enterprise provider configuration. An API key is required when
creating the service.

fields.name: api_key
fields.doc:
Google Gemini Enterprise API key. Required when creating the service.
Supply the value in `api_key.plaintext`.

fields.name: project_id
fields.doc:
GCP project ID hosting the Gemini Enterprise endpoint. Required on
Create.

fields.name: region
fields.doc:
GCP region of the Gemini Enterprise endpoint (e.g., `us-central1`).
Required on Create.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigMicrosoftFoundryProviderConfig
types.doc: Microsoft Foundry provider configuration.

fields.name: direct
fields.doc: Microsoft Foundry endpoint and authentication configuration.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigMicrosoftFoundryProviderDirectConfig
types.doc:
Direct form of Microsoft Foundry provider config.

Authentication is one of three mutually exclusive modes, exactly one of which
must be supplied on Create: - API key: set `api_key`, leave
`entra_service_principal` and `service_credential` unset. - Entra ID (service
principal): set `entra_service_principal`, leave `api_key` and
`service_credential` unset. AI Gateway exchanges these for an Entra bearer
token on outbound requests via the OAuth2 client-credentials grant. - Unity
Catalog service credential: set `service_credential.name` to the resource
name `credentials/{name}`, leave `api_key` and `entra_service_principal`
unset. The credential value lives in Unity Catalog and is referenced by name,
not held on this message. Only supported on Azure-hosted workspaces. Setting
more than one mode is rejected.

fields.name: api_key
fields.doc:
Microsoft Foundry API key. Supply the value in `api_key.plaintext`.
Mutually exclusive with Entra ID and Unity Catalog service credential
authentication.

fields.name: base_url
fields.doc: Microsoft Foundry endpoint URL. Required on Create.

fields.name: entra_service_principal
fields.doc:
Entra ID service-principal authentication. Set `tenant_id`, `client_id`,
and `client_secret.plaintext`. Mutually exclusive with `api_key` and
`service_credential`.

fields.name: service_credential
fields.doc:
Reference to a Unity Catalog service credential authorizing Microsoft
Foundry requests. On Create, supply `service_credential.name` in the form
`credentials/{name}`. Required on Create when using service-credential
authentication; mutually exclusive with `api_key` and
`entra_service_principal`. The credential is referenced by name; its
value is not carried here. Only supported on Azure-hosted workspaces.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigModelTargetConfig
types.doc: Model target configuration for an external model destination.

fields.name: model
fields.doc:
Provider-side model identifier, such as `gpt-5` or `claude-opus-4-7`.
This identifies a model at the upstream provider; it is not a Unity
Catalog model resource.

fields.name: native_api_types
fields.doc:
Provider-native API types supported by this model, such as
`openai/v1/chat/completions`. At least one value is required. AI Gateway
uses these values to translate requests and responses. At most 64 entries
of 256 characters each are allowed.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigOpenAiProviderConfig
types.doc: OpenAI provider configuration.

fields.name: direct
fields.doc: OpenAI configuration with an API key supplied in the request.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigOpenAiProviderDirectConfig
types.doc: Direct (inline-credentials) form of the OpenAI provider config.

fields.name: api_key
fields.doc:
OpenAI API key. Required when creating the service. Supply the value in
`api_key.plaintext`.

fields.name: base_url
fields.doc:
Optional custom base URL. Defaults to `https://api.openai.com/v1`. Use
for OpenAI-API-compatible third-party endpoints or in-network proxies.

fields.name: organization
fields.doc:
Optional OpenAI organization ID. When set, the platform forwards it as
the `OpenAI-Organization` header.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigProviderSecret
types.doc:
A secret value supplied as part of an inline provider config. The caller
supplies the value as inline `plaintext` on writes; the platform stores it
encrypted. The `plaintext` field is `INPUT_ONLY` and never round-trips on
reads.

fields.name: plaintext
fields.doc:
Inline plaintext credential. INPUT_ONLY: the value never round-trips on
reads. Get and List responses omit `plaintext`; the enclosing secret
object remains present to indicate that a secret is configured.

types.name: ModelProviderServiceConfigServiceCredential
types.doc:
The customer-owned Unity Catalog service credential a model provider service
uses to authenticate to its provider, referenced by name.

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
Resource name of the bound Unity Catalog service credential, in the form
`credentials/{name}`. Supply this field when creating the service or
rebinding its credential. On read, it reflects the credential's current
name.

types.name: ModelService
types.doc:
A governed AI Gateway endpoint in Unity Catalog that routes inference
requests to one or more destinations, such as a Databricks foundation model
or an external model reached through a model provider service. Applies
centralized access control, rate limits, and auditing to its traffic.

fields.name: comment
fields.doc: User-provided description.

fields.name: config
fields.doc:
Destinations, routing, rate limits, and payload logging configuration.
Required on Create. On Update, provide this field when `update_mask`
contains `config` or one of its subpaths.

fields.name: create_time
fields.doc: Time the model service was created.

fields.name: created_by
fields.doc: Creator identity.

fields.name: effective_owner
fields.doc: Owner of the model service.

fields.name: etag
fields.doc:
Optimistic concurrency token returned on every read. To make an Update or
Delete conditional, pass the last-read value in that request's `etag`
field. In REST responses, this value is a base64 string; URL-encode it
when setting the `etag` query parameter.

fields.name: metastore_id
fields.doc: Metastore hosting the model service.

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
Resource name of the model service. Format:
`model-services/{catalog}.{schema}.{model_service}`. Each `{...}`
component is capped at 255 characters individually. Server-derived on
Create from `parent` + `model_service_id`; required and immutable on
Update/Get/Delete.

fields.name: supported_api_types
fields.doc:
API types supported across this service's destinations, such as
`openai/v1/chat/completions`, `openai/v1/embeddings`, and
`mlflow/v1/chat/completions`. Derived from the backing models and
providers at read time.

fields.name: update_time
fields.doc: Time the model service was last modified.

fields.name: updated_by
fields.doc: Identity of the last updater.

types.name: ModelServiceConfig
types.doc: Operational configuration wrapped around the ModelService resource.

fields.name: inference_table
fields.doc: Inference table configuration for payload logging.

fields.name: rate_limits
fields.doc: Rate limits applied to requests routed through this model service.

fields.name: routing
fields.doc: Routing configuration: destinations and fallback.

types.name: ModelServiceConfigDestinationConfig
types.doc:
A destination the model service can route traffic to. Exactly one of the
per-type configs inside `type_config` must be set, and it must match
`destination_type`.

fields.name: destination_type
fields.doc:
Backing-model category. Provide the matching type-specific configuration
and leave the other type-specific configurations unset.

fields.name: external_model_config
fields.doc:
Configuration for an external model reached through a model provider
service.

fields.name: is_deleted
fields.doc:
Whether the destination's backing model or model provider service has
been deleted. The destination remains visible so you can identify the
broken dependency. Requests cannot use this destination until the backing
resource is restored or the destination is replaced.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: User-facing label for this destination, used in routing references.

fields.name: pay_per_token_config
fields.doc: Configuration for a pay-per-token Databricks foundation model.

fields.name: provisioned_throughput_config
fields.doc: Configuration for a provisioned-throughput Databricks foundation model.

fields.name: traffic_percentage
fields.doc:
Percentage of primary traffic sent to this destination, from 0 to 100.
Required when there is more than one primary destination, in which case
the primary percentages must sum to 100; a single primary destination
receives all traffic. Fallback destinations are ordered and do not use
this field.

types.name: ModelServiceConfigDestinationConfigDestinationType
types.doc: Backing-model category for a model service destination.

types.name: ModelServiceConfigExternalModelConfig
types.doc:
Configuration for an external-foundation-model destination. Provider auth and
provider-specific cloud configuration are owned by a separate, governed
ModelProviderService entity referenced via `model_provider_service`; the
platform resolves the provider at invocation time.

fields.name: model_provider_service
fields.doc:
Resource name of the governed ModelProviderService that owns provider
auth and provider-specific configuration. The referenced
ModelProviderService also carries the provider type, so this message does
not surface it directly. Format:
`model-provider-services/{catalog}.{schema}.{model_provider_service}`.
Each `{...}` component is capped at 255 characters individually.

fields.name: target
fields.doc:
Routing target for the destination: the provider-side model selected from
the referenced ModelProviderService's `targets` catalog, plus the unified
API types the platform should translate to/from at request time.

types.name: ModelServiceConfigFallbackConfig
types.doc:
Fallback routing applied after a primary destination fails. Fallback
destinations are tried in the listed order.

fields.name: destinations
fields.doc: Fallback destinations, tried in the listed order. At most 5 are allowed.

types.name: ModelServiceConfigPayPerTokenConfig
types.doc:
Configuration for a pay-per-token foundation-model destination. Identifies
the foundation model by its UC resource name; the platform resolves it to a
Model Serving endpoint at request time.

fields.name: model
fields.doc:
Resource name of the Unity Catalog model. Format:
`models/{catalog}.{schema}.{model}`.

types.name: ModelServiceConfigProvisionedThroughputConfig
types.doc:
Configuration for a provisioned-throughput foundation-model destination.
References a pre-existing Model Serving endpoint that serves the model;
sizing (provisioned throughput, burst scaling, model version) is owned by the
Model Serving endpoint itself, not by this message.

fields.name: model
fields.doc:
UC model FQN of the model served by the backing endpoint (e.g.,
`system.ai.databricks-claude-opus-4-6`). Resolved from Model Serving at
Create/Update time.

fields.name: model_serving_endpoint
fields.doc:
Name of the backing Model Serving endpoint serving the provisioned-
throughput foundation model, in the form `serving-endpoints/{name}`. The
same Unity Catalog model can be served on multiple Model Serving
endpoints with different throughput, regions, or configurations. The
caller selects the endpoint to which this destination routes. The
endpoint must exist at create time.

types.name: ModelServiceConfigRoutingConfig
types.doc:
Routing configuration for a model service, nesting destinations and fallback
under a single sub-message.

fields.name: destinations
fields.doc:
Primary routing destinations. At most 10 are allowed. At least one is
required on Create. On Update, provide this list when replacing the full
`config` or updating `config.routing.destinations`; other granular
routing updates do not require resending destinations. The intermediate
`config.routing` mask path is not supported.

fields.name: fallback
fields.doc:
Fallback routing applied after a primary destination fails. Fallback
destinations are tried in the listed order.

fields.name: aliases
fields.doc: List of aliases associated with the model version

fields.name: catalog_name
fields.doc: The name of the catalog containing the model version

fields.name: comment
fields.doc: The comment attached to the model version

fields.name: created_by
fields.doc: The identifier of the user who created the model version

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The unique identifier of the model version

fields.name: metastore_id
fields.doc: The unique identifier of the metastore containing the model version

fields.name: model_name
fields.doc:
The name of the parent registered model of the model version, relative to
parent schema

fields.name: model_version_dependencies
fields.doc: Model version dependencies, for feature-store packaged models

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc:
MLflow run ID used when creating the model version, if ``source`` was
generated by an experiment run stored in an MLflow tracking server

fields.name: run_workspace_id
fields.doc:
ID of the Databricks workspace containing the MLflow run that generated
this model version, if applicable

fields.name: schema_name
fields.doc:
The name of the schema containing the model version, relative to parent
catalog

fields.name: source
fields.doc:
URI indicating the location of the source artifacts (files) for the model
version

fields.name: status
fields.doc:
Current status of the model version. Newly created model versions start
in PENDING_REGISTRATION status, then move to READY status once the model
version files are uploaded and the model version is finalized. Only model
versions in READY status can be loaded for inference or served.

fields.name: storage_location
fields.doc:
The storage location on the cloud under which model version data files
are stored

fields.name: updated_by
fields.doc: The identifier of the user who updated the model version last time

fields.name: version
fields.doc:
Integer model version number, used to reference the model version in API
requests.

fields.name: pause_status
fields.doc: Read only field that indicates whether a schedule is paused or not.

fields.name: quartz_cron_expression
fields.doc:
The expression that determines when to run the monitor. See [examples].

[examples]: https://www.quartz-scheduler.org/documentation/quartz-2.3.0/tutorials/crontrigger.html

fields.name: timezone_id
fields.doc:
The timezone id (e.g., ``PST``) in which to evaluate the quartz
expression.

types.name: MonitorCronSchedulePauseStatus
types.doc:
Source link:
https://src.dev.databricks.com/databricks/universe/-/blob/elastic-spark-common/api/messages/schedule.proto
Monitoring workflow schedule pause status.

types.name: MonitorDataClassificationConfig
types.doc: Data classification related configuration.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether to enable data classification.

fields.name: email_addresses
fields.doc:
The list of email addresses to send the notification to. A maximum of 5
email addresses is supported.

fields.name: granularities
fields.doc:
List of granularities to use when aggregating data into time windows
based on their timestamp.

fields.name: label_col
fields.doc: Column for the label.

fields.name: model_id_col
fields.doc: Column for the model identifier.

fields.name: prediction_col
fields.doc: Column for the prediction.

fields.name: prediction_proba_col
fields.doc: Column for prediction probabilities

fields.name: problem_type
fields.doc: Problem type the model aims to solve.

fields.name: timestamp_col
fields.doc: Column for the timestamp.

fields.name: assets_dir
fields.doc:
[Create:REQ Update:IGN] Field for specifying the absolute path to a
custom directory to store data-monitoring assets. Normally prepopulated
to a default user location via UI and Python APIs.

fields.name: baseline_table_name
fields.doc:
[Create:OPT Update:OPT] Baseline table name. Baseline data is used to
compute drift from the data in the monitored `table_name`. The baseline
table and the monitored table shall have the same schema.

fields.name: custom_metrics
fields.doc: [Create:OPT Update:OPT] Custom metrics.

fields.name: dashboard_id
fields.doc:
[Create:ERR Update:OPT] Id of dashboard that visualizes the computed
metrics. This can be empty if the monitor is in PENDING state.

fields.name: data_classification_config
fields.doc: [Create:OPT Update:OPT] Data classification related config.

fields.name: drift_metrics_table_name
fields.doc:
[Create:ERR Update:IGN] Table that stores drift metrics data. Format:
`catalog.schema.table_name`.

fields.name: latest_monitor_failure_msg
fields.doc: [Create:ERR Update:IGN] The latest error message for a monitor failure.

fields.name: monitor_version
fields.doc:
[Create:ERR Update:IGN] Represents the current monitor configuration
version in use. The version will be represented in a numeric fashion
(1,2,3...). The field has flexibility to take on negative values, which
can indicate corrupted monitor_version numbers.

fields.name: notifications
fields.doc: [Create:OPT Update:OPT] Field for specifying notification settings.

fields.name: output_schema_name
fields.doc:
[Create:REQ Update:REQ] Schema where output tables are created. Needs to
be in 2-level format {catalog}.{schema}

fields.name: profile_metrics_table_name
fields.doc:
[Create:ERR Update:IGN] Table that stores profile metrics data. Format:
`catalog.schema.table_name`.

fields.name: schedule
fields.doc: [Create:OPT Update:OPT] The monitor schedule.

fields.name: slicing_exprs
fields.doc:
[Create:OPT Update:OPT] List of column expressions to slice data with for
targeted analysis. The data is grouped by each expression independently,
resulting in a separate slice for each predicate and its complements. For
example `slicing_exprs=[“col_1”, “col_2 > 10”]` will generate the
following slices: two slices for `col_2 > 10` (True and False), and one
slice per unique value in `col1`. For high-cardinality columns, only the
top 100 unique values by frequency will generate slices.

fields.name: snapshot
fields.doc: Configuration for monitoring snapshot tables.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: [Create:ERR Update:IGN] The monitor status.

fields.name: table_name

[Create:ERR Update:IGN] UC table to monitor. Format:
`catalog.schema.table_name`

fields.name: time_series
fields.doc: Configuration for monitoring time series tables.

types.name: MonitorMetric
types.doc: Custom metric definition.

fields.name: definition
fields.doc:
Jinja template for a SQL expression that specifies how to compute the
metric. See [create metric definition].

[create metric definition]: https://docs.databricks.com/en/lakehouse-monitoring/custom-metrics.html#create-definition

fields.name: input_columns
fields.doc:
A list of column names in the input table the metric should be computed
for. Can use ``":table"`` to indicate that the metric needs information
from multiple columns.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Name of the metric in the output tables.

fields.name: output_data_type
fields.doc: The output type of the custom metric.

fields.name: type
fields.doc:
Can only be one of ``"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_AGGREGATE"``,
``"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DERIVED"``, or ``"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DRIFT"``. The
``"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_AGGREGATE"`` and ``"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DERIVED"``
metrics are computed on a single table, whereas the
``"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DRIFT"`` compare metrics across baseline and input
table, or across the two consecutive time windows. -
CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_AGGREGATE: only depend on the existing columns in your
table - CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DERIVED: depend on previously computed
aggregate metrics - CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DRIFT: depend on previously
computed aggregate or derived metrics

types.name: MonitorMetricType
types.doc:
Can only be one of “\"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_AGGREGATE\"“,
“\"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DERIVED\"“, or “\"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DRIFT\"“. The
“\"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_AGGREGATE\"“ and “\"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DERIVED\"“
metrics are computed on a single table, whereas the
“\"CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DRIFT\"“ compare metrics across baseline and input
table, or across the two consecutive time windows. -
CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_AGGREGATE: only depend on the existing columns in your
table - CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DERIVED: depend on previously computed aggregate
metrics - CUSTOM_METRIC_TYPE_DRIFT: depend on previously computed aggregate
or derived metrics

fields.name: on_failure
fields.doc: Destinations to send notifications on failure/timeout.

fields.name: on_new_classification_tag_detected
fields.doc: Destinations to send notifications on new classification tag detected.

fields.name: end_time_ms
fields.doc:
Time at which refresh operation completed (milliseconds since 1/1/1970
UTC).

fields.name: message
fields.doc:
An optional message to give insight into the current state of the job
(e.g. FAILURE messages).

fields.name: refresh_id
fields.doc: Unique id of the refresh operation.

fields.name: start_time_ms
fields.doc:
Time at which refresh operation was initiated (milliseconds since
1/1/1970 UTC).

fields.name: state
fields.doc: The current state of the refresh.

fields.name: trigger
fields.doc: The method by which the refresh was triggered.

types.name: MonitorRefreshInfoState
types.doc: The current state of the refresh.

fields.name: refreshes
fields.doc: List of refreshes.

types.name: MonitorSnapshot
types.doc: Snapshot analysis configuration

types.name: MonitorTimeSeries
types.doc: Time series analysis configuration.

fields.name: granularities
fields.doc:
Granularities for aggregating data into time windows based on their
timestamp. Currently the following static granularities are supported:
{``\"5 minutes\"``, ``\"30 minutes\"``, ``\"1 hour\"``, ``\"1 day\"``,
``\"\u003cn\u003e week(s)\"``, ``\"1 month\"``, ``\"1 year\"``}.

fields.name: timestamp_col
fields.doc: Column for the timestamp.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The name of the constraint.

fields.name: destination_id
fields.doc:
The identifier for the destination. This is the email address for EMAIL
destinations, the URL for URL destinations, or the unique Databricks
notification destination ID for all other external destinations.

fields.name: destination_type
fields.doc: The type of the destination.

fields.name: special_destination
fields.doc:
This field is used to denote whether the destination is the email of the
owner of the securable object. The special destination cannot be assigned
to a securable and only represents the default destination of the
securable. The securable types that support default special destinations
are: "catalog", "external_location", "connection", "credential", and
"metastore". The **destination_type** of a **special_destination** is
always EMAIL.

types.name: OnlineTable
types.doc: Online Table information.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Full three-part (catalog, schema, table) name of the table.

fields.name: spec
fields.doc: Specification of the online table.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Online Table data synchronization status

fields.name: table_serving_url
fields.doc: Data serving REST API URL for this table

fields.name: unity_catalog_provisioning_state
fields.doc:
The provisioning state of the online table entity in Unity Catalog. This
is distinct from the state of the data synchronization pipeline (i.e. the
table may be in "ACTIVE" but the pipeline may be in "PROVISIONING" as it
runs asynchronously).

types.name: OnlineTableSpec
types.doc: Specification of an online table.

fields.name: perform_full_copy
fields.doc:
Whether to create a full-copy pipeline -- a pipeline that stops after
creates a full copy of the source table upon initialization and does not
process any change data feeds (CDFs) afterwards. The pipeline can still
be manually triggered afterwards, but it always perform a full copy of
the source table and there are no incremental updates. This mode is
useful for syncing views or tables without CDFs to online tables. Note
that the full-copy pipeline only supports "triggered" scheduling policy.

fields.name: pipeline_id
fields.doc:
ID of the associated pipeline. Generated by the server - cannot be set by
the caller.

fields.name: primary_key_columns
fields.doc: Primary Key columns to be used for data insert/update in the destination.

fields.name: run_continuously
fields.doc: Pipeline runs continuously after generating the initial data.

fields.name: run_triggered
fields.doc:
Pipeline stops after generating the initial data and can be triggered
later (manually, through a cron job or through data triggers)

fields.name: source_table_full_name
fields.doc: Three-part (catalog, schema, table) name of the source Delta table.

fields.name: timeseries_key
fields.doc:
Time series key to deduplicate (tie-break) rows with the same primary
key.

types.name: OnlineTableState
types.doc: The state of an online table.

types.name: OnlineTableStatus
types.doc: Status of an online table.

fields.name: detailed_state
fields.doc: The state of the online table.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: A text description of the current state of the online table.

types.name: OptionSpec
types.doc:
Spec of an allowed option on a securable kind and its attributes. This is
mostly used by UI to provide user friendly hints and descriptions in order to
facilitate the securable creation process.

fields.name: allowed_values
fields.doc:
For drop down / radio button selections, UI will want to know the
possible input values, it can also be used by other option types to limit
input selections.

fields.name: default_value
fields.doc:
The default value of the option, for example, value '443' for 'port'
option.

fields.name: description
fields.doc:
A concise user facing description of what the input value of this option
should look like.

fields.name: hint
fields.doc:
The hint is used on the UI to suggest what the input value can possibly
be like, for example: example.com for 'host' option. Unlike default
value, it will not be applied automatically without user input.

fields.name: is_copiable
fields.doc:
Indicates whether an option should be displayed with copy button on the
UI.

fields.name: is_creatable
fields.doc:
Indicates whether an option can be provided by users in the create/update
path of an entity.

fields.name: is_hidden
fields.doc: Is the option value not user settable and is thus not shown on the UI.

fields.name: is_loggable
fields.doc:
Specifies whether this option is safe to log, i.e. no sensitive
information.

fields.name: is_required
fields.doc: Is the option required.

fields.name: is_secret
fields.doc: Is the option value considered secret and thus redacted on the UI.

fields.name: is_updatable
fields.doc: Is the option updatable by users.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The unique name of the option.

fields.name: oauth_stage
fields.doc:
Specifies when the option value is displayed on the UI within the OAuth
flow.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: The type of the option.

types.name: OptionSpecOauthStage
types.doc:
During the OAuth flow, specifies which stage the option should be displayed
in the UI. OAUTH_STAGE_UNSPECIFIED is the default value for options unrelated
to the OAuth flow. BEFORE_AUTHORIZATION_CODE corresponds to options necessary
to initiate the OAuth process. BEFORE_ACCESS_TOKEN corresponds to options
that are necessary to create a foreign connection, but that should be
displayed after the authorization code has already been received.

types.name: OptionSpecOptionType
types.doc:
Type of the option, we purposely follow JavaScript types so that the UI can
map the options to JS types. https://www.w3schools.com/js/js_datatypes.asp
Enum is a special case that it's just string with selections.

fields.name: add
fields.doc: The set of privileges to add.

fields.name: principal
fields.doc:
The principal whose privileges we are changing. Only one of principal or
principal_id should be specified, never both at the same time.

fields.name: remove
fields.doc: The set of privileges to remove.

types.name: PipelineProgress
types.doc: Progress information of the Online Table data synchronization pipeline.

fields.name: estimated_completion_time_seconds
fields.doc: The estimated time remaining to complete this update in seconds.

fields.name: latest_version_currently_processing
fields.doc:
The source table Delta version that was last processed by the pipeline.
The pipeline may not have completely processed this version yet.

fields.name: sync_progress_completion
fields.doc: The completion ratio of this update. This is a number between 0 and 1.

fields.name: synced_row_count
fields.doc: The number of rows that have been synced in this update.

fields.name: total_row_count
fields.doc:
The total number of rows that need to be synced in this update. This
number may be an estimate.

types.name: PolicyFunctionArgument
types.doc:
A positional argument passed to a row filter or column mask function.
Distinguishes between column references and literals.

fields.name: column
fields.doc: A column reference.

fields.name: constant
fields.doc: A constant literal.

fields.name: column_mask
fields.doc:
Options for column mask policies. Valid only if `policy_type` is
`POLICY_TYPE_COLUMN_MASK`. Required on create and optional on update.
When specified on update, the new options will replace the existing
options as a whole.

fields.name: comment
fields.doc: Optional description of the policy.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: Time at which the policy was created, in epoch milliseconds. Output only.

fields.name: created_by
fields.doc: Username of the user who created the policy. Output only.

fields.name: deny
fields.doc:
Options for deny policies. Valid only if `policy_type` is
`POLICY_TYPE_DENY`. Required on create and optional on update. When
specified on update, the new options will replace the existing options as
a whole.

fields.name: except_principals
fields.doc:
Optional list of user or group names that should be excluded from the
policy.

fields.name: for_securable_type
fields.doc:
Type of securables that the policy should take effect on. Required on
create and optional on update.

fields.name: grant
fields.doc:
Options for grant policies. Valid only if `policy_type` is
`POLICY_TYPE_GRANT`. Required on create and optional on update. When
specified on update, the new options will replace the existing options as
a whole.

fields.name: id
fields.doc:
Unique identifier of the policy. This field is output only and is
generated by the system.

fields.name: match_columns
fields.doc:
Optional list of condition expressions used to match table columns. Only
valid when `for_securable_type` is `TABLE`. When specified, the policy
only applies to tables whose columns satisfy all match conditions.

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
Name of the policy. Required on create and optional on update. To rename
the policy, set `name` to a different value on update.

fields.name: on_securable_fullname
fields.doc:
Full name of the securable on which the policy is defined. Required on
create.

fields.name: on_securable_type
fields.doc:
Type of the securable on which the policy is defined. Only `CATALOG`,
`SCHEMA` and `TABLE` are supported at this moment. Required on create.

fields.name: policy_type
fields.doc: Type of the policy. Required on create.

fields.name: row_filter
fields.doc:
Options for row filter policies. Valid only if `policy_type` is
`POLICY_TYPE_ROW_FILTER`. Required on create and optional on update. When
specified on update, the new options will replace the existing options as
a whole.

fields.name: to_principals
fields.doc:
List of user or group names that the policy applies to. Required on
create and optional on update.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.doc:
Time at which the policy was last modified, in epoch milliseconds. Output
only.

fields.name: updated_by
fields.doc: Username of the user who last modified the policy. Output only.

fields.name: when_condition
fields.doc: Optional condition when the policy should take effect.

fields.name: child_columns
fields.doc: Column names for this constraint.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The name of the constraint.

fields.name: rely
fields.doc: True if the constraint is RELY, false or unset if NORELY.

fields.name: timeseries_columns
fields.doc: Column names that represent a timeseries.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Databricks user, group or service principal ID.

fields.name: principal
fields.doc:
The principal (user email address or group name). For deleted principals,
`principal` is empty while `principal_id` is populated.

fields.name: privileges
fields.doc: The privileges assigned to the principal.

types.name: ProvisioningInfo

fields.name: state
fields.doc: The provisioning state of the resource.

types.name: ProvisioningStatus

Detailed status of an online table. Shown if the online table is in the
PROVISIONING_PIPELINE_RESOURCES or the PROVISIONING_INITIAL_SNAPSHOT state.

fields.name: initial_pipeline_sync_progress
fields.doc:
Details about initial data synchronization. Only populated when in the
PROVISIONING_INITIAL_SNAPSHOT state.

fields.name: last_refreshed_at

fields.name: parent_full_name

fields.name: quota_limit

types.name: R2Credentials
types.doc:
R2 temporary credentials for API authentication. Read more at
https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/tokens/.

fields.name: access_key_id
fields.doc: The access key ID that identifies the temporary credentials.

fields.name: secret_access_key

fields.name: session_token
fields.doc: The generated JWT that users must pass to use the temporary credentials.

types.name: RateLimit
types.doc:
A rate limit applied to service requests. Leave `requests` or `tokens` unset
to impose no limit on that dimension; set a value to cap that dimension
within the renewal period.

fields.name: key
fields.doc:
Scope of the rate limit. Depending on this value, the limit applies to a
principal, the service as a whole, or each user by default.

fields.name: principal
fields.doc:
Principal this limit applies to: user email, group name, or service
principal application ID. Required when `key` applies to a user, group,
or service principal; otherwise it must be unset.

fields.name: renewal_period
fields.doc: Renewal period.

fields.name: requests
fields.doc:
Maximum requests allowed in one renewal period. Leave unset for no
request limit. Set to `0` to deny all requests.

fields.name: tokens
fields.doc:
Maximum tokens allowed in one renewal period. Leave unset for no token
limit. Set to `0` to deny all requests.

types.name: RateLimitRateLimitKey

types.name: RateLimitRateLimitRenewalPeriod
types.doc: Renewal period for a rate limit.

match the positional argument of the row filter function.

fields.name: table_name

fields.name: browse_only

Indicates whether the principal is limited to retrieving metadata for the

fields.name: enable_predictive_optimization

fields.name: updated_at

fields.name: updated_by

types.name: Secret
types.doc:
A secret stored in Unity Catalog. Secrets are three-level namespace objects
(catalog.schema.secret) that securely store sensitive credential data such as
passwords, tokens, and keys.

fields.name: catalog_name
fields.doc: The name of the catalog where the schema and the secret reside.

fields.name: comment
fields.doc: User-provided free-form text description of the secret.

fields.name: create_time
fields.doc: The time at which this secret was created.

fields.name: created_by
fields.doc: The principal that created the secret.

fields.name: effective_owner
fields.doc:
The effective owner of the secret, which may differ from the directly-set
**owner** due to inheritance.

fields.name: effective_value
fields.doc:
The secret value. Only populated in responses when you have the
**READ_SECRET** privilege and **include_value** is set to true in the
request. The maximum size is 60 KiB.

fields.name: expire_time
fields.doc:
User-provided expiration time of the secret. This field indicates when
the secret should no longer be used and may be displayed as a warning in
the UI. It is purely informational and does not trigger any automatic
actions or affect the secret's lifecycle.

fields.name: full_name
fields.doc:
The three-level (fully qualified) name of the secret, in the form of
**catalog_name.schema_name.secret_name**.

fields.name: metastore_id
fields.doc: Unique identifier of the metastore hosting the secret.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The name of the secret, relative to its parent schema.

fields.name: owner
fields.doc:
The owner of the secret. Defaults to the creating principal on creation.
Can be updated to transfer ownership of the secret to another principal.

fields.name: schema_name
fields.doc: The name of the schema where the secret resides.

fields.name: update_time
fields.doc: The time at which this secret was last updated.

fields.name: updated_by
fields.doc: The principal that last updated the secret.

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The secret value to store. This field is input-only and is not returned
in responses — use the **effective_value** field (via GetSecret with
**include_value** set to true) to read the secret value. The maximum size
is 60 KiB (pre-encryption). Accepted content includes passwords, tokens,
keys, and other sensitive credential data.

fields.doc:
The AWS IAM role ARN of the role associated with the instance profile.
This field is required if your role name and instance profile name do not
match and you want to use the instance profile with [Databricks SQL
Serverless].

Otherwise, this field is optional.

[Databricks SQL Serverless]: https://docs.databricks.com/sql/admin/serverless.html

fields.name: instance_profile_arn
fields.doc:
The AWS ARN of the instance profile to register with Databricks. This
field is required.

fields.name: is_meta_instance_profile
fields.doc:
Boolean flag indicating whether the instance profile should only be used
in credential passthrough scenarios. If true, it means the instance
profile contains an meta IAM role which could assume a wide range of
roles. Therefore it should always be used with authorization. This field
is optional, the default value is `false`.

fields.name: skip_validation
fields.doc:
By default, Databricks validates that it has sufficient permissions to
launch instances with the instance profile. This validation uses AWS
dry-run mode for the RunInstances API. If validation fails with an error
message that does not indicate an IAM related permission issue, (e.g.
“Your requested instance type is not supported in your requested
availability zone”), you can pass this flag to skip the validation and
forcibly add the instance profile.

types.doc: A storage location in Adls Gen2

fields.name: destination
fields.doc:
abfss destination, e.g.
`abfss://<container-name>@<storage-account-name>.dfs.core.windows.net/<directory-name>`.

fields.name: max_workers
fields.doc:
The maximum number of workers to which the cluster can scale up when
overloaded. Note that `max_workers` must be strictly greater than
`min_workers`.

fields.name: min_workers
fields.doc:
The minimum number of workers to which the cluster can scale down when
underutilized. It is also the initial number of workers the cluster will
have after creation.

types.name: AwsAttributes
types.doc:
Attributes set during cluster creation which are related to Amazon Web
Services.

fields.name: ebs_volume_count
fields.doc:
The number of volumes launched for each instance. Users can choose up to
10 volumes. This feature is only enabled for supported node types. Legacy
node types cannot specify custom EBS volumes. For node types with no
instance store, at least one EBS volume needs to be specified; otherwise,
cluster creation will fail.

These EBS volumes will be mounted at `/ebs0`, `/ebs1`, and etc. Instance
store volumes will be mounted at `/local_disk0`, `/local_disk1`, and etc.

If EBS volumes are attached, Databricks will configure Spark to use only
the EBS volumes for scratch storage because heterogenously sized scratch
devices can lead to inefficient disk utilization. If no EBS volumes are
attached, Databricks will configure Spark to use instance store volumes.

Please note that if EBS volumes are specified, then the Spark
configuration `spark.local.dir` will be overridden.

fields.name: ebs_volume_iops
fields.doc:
If using gp3 volumes, what IOPS to use for the disk. If this is not set,
the maximum performance of a gp2 volume with the same volume size will be
used.

fields.name: ebs_volume_size
fields.doc:
The size of each EBS volume (in GiB) launched for each instance. For
general purpose SSD, this value must be within the range 100 - 4096. For
throughput optimized HDD, this value must be within the range 500 - 4096.

fields.name: ebs_volume_throughput
fields.doc:
If using gp3 volumes, what throughput to use for the disk. If this is not
set, the maximum performance of a gp2 volume with the same volume size
will be used.

fields.name: ebs_volume_type
fields.doc: The type of EBS volumes that will be launched with this cluster.

fields.name: first_on_demand
fields.doc:
The first `first_on_demand` nodes of the cluster will be placed on
on-demand instances. If this value is greater than 0, the cluster driver
node in particular will be placed on an on-demand instance. If this value
is greater than or equal to the current cluster size, all nodes will be
placed on on-demand instances. If this value is less than the current
cluster size, `first_on_demand` nodes will be placed on on-demand
instances and the remainder will be placed on `availability` instances.
Note that this value does not affect cluster size and cannot currently be
mutated over the lifetime of a cluster.

fields.name: instance_profile_arn
fields.doc:
Nodes for this cluster will only be placed on AWS instances with this
instance profile. If ommitted, nodes will be placed on instances without
an IAM instance profile. The instance profile must have previously been
added to the Databricks environment by an account administrator.

This feature may only be available to certain customer plans.

fields.name: spot_bid_price_percent
fields.doc:
The bid price for AWS spot instances, as a percentage of the
corresponding instance type's on-demand price. For example, if this field
is set to 50, and the cluster needs a new `r3.xlarge` spot instance, then
the bid price is half of the price of on-demand `r3.xlarge` instances.
Similarly, if this field is set to 200, the bid price is twice the price
of on-demand `r3.xlarge` instances. If not specified, the default value
is 100. When spot instances are requested for this cluster, only spot
instances whose bid price percentage matches this field will be
considered. Note that, for safety, we enforce this field to be no more
than 10000.

fields.name: zone_id
fields.doc:
Identifier for the availability zone/datacenter in which the cluster
resides. This string will be of a form like "us-west-2a". The provided
availability zone must be in the same region as the Databricks
deployment. For example, "us-west-2a" is not a valid zone id if the
Databricks deployment resides in the "us-east-1" region. This is an
optional field at cluster creation, and if not specified, the zone "auto"
will be used. If the zone specified is "auto", will try to place cluster
in a zone with high availability, and will retry placement in a different
AZ if there is not enough capacity.

The list of available zones as well as the default value can be found by
using the `List Zones` method.

types.name: AwsAvailability
types.doc:
Availability type used for all subsequent nodes past the `first_on_demand`
ones.

Note: If `first_on_demand` is zero, this availability type will be used for
the entire cluster.

types.name: AzureAttributes
types.doc: Attributes set during cluster creation which are related to Microsoft Azure.

fields.name: availability
fields.doc:
Availability type used for all subsequent nodes past the
`first_on_demand` ones. Note: If `first_on_demand` is zero, this
availability type will be used for the entire cluster.

fields.name: capacity_reservation_group
fields.doc:
The Azure capacity reservation group resource ID to use for launching
VMs. When specified, VMs will be launched using the provided capacity
reservation.

Capacity reservations can only be specified when the workspace uses
injected vnet (i.e. customer defined vnet not managed by databricks).
Ensure the databricks-login-prod Enterprise Application is granted the
following four permissions: 1.
Microsoft.Compute/capacityReservationGroups/read 2.
Microsoft.Compute/capacityReservationGroups/deploy/action 3.
Microsoft.Compute/capacityReservationGroups/capacityReservations/read 4.
Microsoft.Compute/capacityReservationGroups/capacityReservations/deploy/action

Format:
`/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.Compute/capacityReservationGroups/{capacityReservationGroupName}`

fields.name: first_on_demand
fields.doc:
The first `first_on_demand` nodes of the cluster will be placed on
on-demand instances. This value should be greater than 0, to make sure
the cluster driver node is placed on an on-demand instance. If this value
is greater than or equal to the current cluster size, all nodes will be
placed on on-demand instances. If this value is less than the current
cluster size, `first_on_demand` nodes will be placed on on-demand
instances and the remainder will be placed on `availability` instances.
Note that this value does not affect cluster size and cannot currently be
mutated over the lifetime of a cluster.

fields.name: log_analytics_info
fields.doc: Defines values necessary to configure and run Azure Log Analytics agent

fields.name: spot_bid_max_price
fields.doc:
The max bid price to be used for Azure spot instances. The Max price for
the bid cannot be higher than the on-demand price of the instance. If not
specified, the default value is -1, which specifies that the instance
cannot be evicted on the basis of price, and only on the basis of
availability. Further, the value should > 0 or -1.

types.name: AzureAvailability
types.doc:
Availability type used for all subsequent nodes past the `first_on_demand`
ones. Note: If `first_on_demand` is zero, this availability type will be used
for the entire cluster.

types.name: ClusterAttributes
types.doc:
Common set of attributes set during cluster creation. These attributes cannot
be changed over the lifetime of a cluster.

fields.name: autotermination_minutes
fields.doc:
Automatically terminates the cluster after it is inactive for this time
in minutes. If not set, this cluster will not be automatically
terminated. If specified, the threshold must be between 10 and 10000
minutes. Users can also set this value to 0 to explicitly disable
automatic termination.

fields.name: aws_attributes
fields.doc:
Attributes related to clusters running on Amazon Web Services. If not
specified at cluster creation, a set of default values will be used.

fields.name: azure_attributes
fields.doc:
Attributes related to clusters running on Microsoft Azure. If not
specified at cluster creation, a set of default values will be used.

fields.name: cluster_log_conf
fields.doc:
The configuration for delivering spark logs to a long-term storage
destination. Three kinds of destinations (DBFS, S3 and Unity Catalog
volumes) are supported. Only one destination can be specified for one
cluster. If the conf is given, the logs will be delivered to the
destination every `5 mins`. The destination of driver logs is
`$destination/$clusterId/driver`, while the destination of executor logs
is `$destination/$clusterId/executor`.

fields.name: cluster_name
fields.doc:
Cluster name requested by the user. This doesn't have to be unique. If
not specified at creation, the cluster name will be an empty string. For
job clusters, the cluster name is automatically set based on the job and
job run IDs.

fields.name: custom_tags
fields.doc:
Additional tags for cluster resources. Databricks will tag all cluster
resources (e.g., AWS instances and EBS volumes) with these tags in
addition to `default_tags`. Notes:

- Currently, Databricks allows at most 45 custom tags

- Clusters can only reuse cloud resources if the resources' tags are a
subset of the cluster tags

fields.name: dependency_mode
fields.doc: Controls dependency configuration for the cluster.

fields.name: docker_image
fields.doc: Custom docker image BYOC

fields.name: driver_instance_pool_id
fields.doc:
The optional ID of the instance pool for the driver of the cluster
belongs. The pool cluster uses the instance pool with id
(instance_pool_id) if the driver pool is not assigned.

fields.name: driver_node_type_flexibility
fields.doc: Flexible node type configuration for the driver node.

fields.name: driver_node_type_id
fields.doc:
The node type of the Spark driver. Note that this field is optional; if
unset, the driver node type will be set as the same value as
`node_type_id` defined above.

This field, along with node_type_id, should not be set if
virtual_cluster_size is set. If both driver_node_type_id, node_type_id,
and virtual_cluster_size are specified, driver_node_type_id and
node_type_id take precedence.

fields.name: enable_elastic_disk
fields.doc:
Autoscaling Local Storage: when enabled, this cluster will dynamically
acquire additional disk space when its Spark workers are running low on
disk space.

fields.name: enable_local_disk_encryption
fields.doc: Whether to enable LUKS on cluster VMs' local disks

fields.name: gcp_attributes
fields.doc:
Attributes related to clusters running on Google Cloud Platform. If not
specified at cluster creation, a set of default values will be used.

fields.name: init_scripts
fields.doc:
The configuration for storing init scripts. Any number of destinations
can be specified. The scripts are executed sequentially in the order
provided. If `cluster_log_conf` is specified, init script logs are sent
to `<destination>/<cluster-ID>/init_scripts`.

fields.name: instance_pool_id
fields.doc: The optional ID of the instance pool to which the cluster belongs.

fields.name: is_single_node
fields.doc:
This field can only be used when `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.

When set to true, Databricks will automatically set single node related
`custom_tags`, `spark_conf`, and `num_workers`

fields.name: node_type_id
fields.doc:
This field encodes, through a single value, the resources available to
each of the Spark nodes in this cluster. For example, the Spark nodes can
be provisioned and optimized for memory or compute intensive workloads. A
list of available node types can be retrieved by using the
[clusters/listNodeTypes] API call.

[clusters/listNodeTypes]: https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/clusters/listnodetypes

fields.name: policy_id
fields.doc: The ID of the cluster policy used to create the cluster if applicable.

fields.name: remote_disk_throughput
fields.doc:
If set, what the configurable throughput (in Mb/s) for the remote disk
is. Currently only supported for GCP HYPERDISK_BALANCED disks.

fields.name: runtime_engine
fields.doc:
Determines the cluster's runtime engine, either standard or Photon.

This field is not compatible with legacy `spark_version` values that
contain `-photon-`. Remove `-photon-` from the `spark_version` and set
`runtime_engine` to `PHOTON`.

If left unspecified, the runtime engine defaults to standard unless the
spark_version contains -photon-, in which case Photon will be used.

fields.name: single_user_name
fields.doc: Single user name if data_security_mode is `SINGLE_USER`

fields.name: spark_conf
fields.doc:
An object containing a set of optional, user-specified Spark
configuration key-value pairs. Users can also pass in a string of extra
JVM options to the driver and the executors via
`spark.driver.extraJavaOptions` and `spark.executor.extraJavaOptions`
respectively.

fields.name: spark_env_vars
fields.doc:
An object containing a set of optional, user-specified environment
variable key-value pairs. Please note that key-value pair of the form
(X,Y) will be exported as is (i.e., `export X='Y'`) while launching the
driver and workers.

In order to specify an additional set of `SPARK_DAEMON_JAVA_OPTS`, we
recommend appending them to `$SPARK_DAEMON_JAVA_OPTS` as shown in the
example below. This ensures that all default databricks managed
environmental variables are included as well.

Example Spark environment variables: `{"SPARK_WORKER_MEMORY": "28000m",
"SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS": "/local_disk0"}` or `{"SPARK_DAEMON_JAVA_OPTS":
"$SPARK_DAEMON_JAVA_OPTS -Dspark.shuffle.service.enabled=true"}`

fields.name: spark_version
fields.doc:
The Spark version of the cluster, e.g. `3.3.x-scala2.11`. A list of
available Spark versions can be retrieved by using the
[clusters/sparkVersions] API call.

[clusters/sparkVersions]: https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/clusters/sparkversions

fields.name: ssh_public_keys
fields.doc:
SSH public key contents that will be added to each Spark node in this
cluster. The corresponding private keys can be used to login with the
user name `ubuntu` on port `2200`. Up to 10 keys can be specified.

fields.name: total_initial_remote_disk_size
fields.doc:
If set, what the total initial volume size (in GB) of the remote disks
should be. Supported for GCP.

fields.name: use_ml_runtime
fields.doc:
This field can only be used when `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.

`effective_spark_version` is determined by `spark_version` (DBR release),
this field `use_ml_runtime`, and whether `node_type_id` is gpu node or
not.

fields.name: worker_node_type_flexibility
fields.doc: Flexible node type configuration for worker nodes.

fields.name: cluster_id
fields.doc: Canonical unique identifier for a cluster.

fields.name: is_compliant
fields.doc:
Whether this cluster is in compliance with the latest version of its
policy.

fields.name: pending_enforcement
fields.doc:
Information about the pending enforcement for the cluster. Only present
if a pending enforcement is scheduled for the cluster.

fields.name: violations
fields.doc:
An object containing key-value mappings representing the first 200 policy
validation errors. The keys indicate the path where the policy validation
error is occurring. The values indicate an error message describing the
policy validation error.

types.name: ClusterDetails
types.doc: Describes all of the metadata about a single Spark cluster in Databricks.

fields.name: autoscale
fields.doc:
Parameters needed in order to automatically scale clusters up and down
based on load. Note: autoscaling works best with DB runtime versions 3.0
or later.

fields.name: autotermination_minutes
fields.doc:
Automatically terminates the cluster after it is inactive for this time
in minutes. If not set, this cluster will not be automatically
terminated. If specified, the threshold must be between 10 and 10000
minutes. Users can also set this value to 0 to explicitly disable
automatic termination.

fields.name: aws_attributes
fields.doc:
Attributes related to clusters running on Amazon Web Services. If not
specified at cluster creation, a set of default values will be used.

fields.name: azure_attributes
fields.doc:
Attributes related to clusters running on Microsoft Azure. If not
specified at cluster creation, a set of default values will be used.

fields.name: cluster_cores
fields.doc:
Number of CPU cores available for this cluster. Note that this can be
fractional, e.g. 7.5 cores, since certain node types are configured to
share cores between Spark nodes on the same instance.

fields.name: cluster_id
fields.doc:
Canonical identifier for the cluster. This id is retained during cluster
restarts and resizes, while each new cluster has a globally unique id.

fields.name: cluster_log_conf
fields.doc:
The configuration for delivering spark logs to a long-term storage
destination. Three kinds of destinations (DBFS, S3 and Unity Catalog
volumes) are supported. Only one destination can be specified for one
cluster. If the conf is given, the logs will be delivered to the
destination every `5 mins`. The destination of driver logs is
`$destination/$clusterId/driver`, while the destination of executor logs
is `$destination/$clusterId/executor`.

fields.name: cluster_log_status

fields.name: cluster_memory_mb
fields.doc: Total amount of cluster memory, in megabytes

fields.name: cluster_name
fields.doc:
Cluster name requested by the user. This doesn't have to be unique. If
not specified at creation, the cluster name will be an empty string. For
job clusters, the cluster name is automatically set based on the job and
job run IDs.

fields.name: cluster_source
fields.doc:
Determines whether the cluster was created by a user through the UI,
created by the Databricks Jobs Scheduler, or through an API request.

fields.name: creator_user_name
fields.doc:
Creator user name. The field won't be included in the response if the
user has already been deleted.

fields.name: custom_tags
fields.doc:
Additional tags for cluster resources. Databricks will tag all cluster
resources (e.g., AWS instances and EBS volumes) with these tags in
addition to `default_tags`. Notes:

- Currently, Databricks allows at most 45 custom tags

- Clusters can only reuse cloud resources if the resources' tags are a
subset of the cluster tags

fields.name: default_tags

including:

- Vendor: Databricks

- Creator: <username_of_creator>

- ClusterName: <name_of_cluster>

- ClusterId: <id_of_cluster>

- Name: <Databricks internal use>

fields.name: dependency_mode
fields.doc: Controls dependency configuration for the cluster.

fields.name: docker_image
fields.doc: Custom docker image BYOC

fields.name: driver
fields.doc:
Node on which the Spark driver resides. The driver node contains the
Spark master and the Databricks application that manages the per-notebook
Spark REPLs.

fields.name: driver_instance_pool_id
fields.doc:
The optional ID of the instance pool for the driver of the cluster
belongs. The pool cluster uses the instance pool with id
(instance_pool_id) if the driver pool is not assigned.

fields.name: driver_node_type_flexibility
fields.doc: Flexible node type configuration for the driver node.

fields.name: driver_node_type_id
fields.doc:
The node type of the Spark driver. Note that this field is optional; if
unset, the driver node type will be set as the same value as
`node_type_id` defined above.

This field, along with node_type_id, should not be set if
virtual_cluster_size is set. If both driver_node_type_id, node_type_id,
and virtual_cluster_size are specified, driver_node_type_id and
node_type_id take precedence.

fields.name: enable_elastic_disk
fields.doc:
Autoscaling Local Storage: when enabled, this cluster will dynamically
acquire additional disk space when its Spark workers are running low on
disk space.

fields.name: enable_local_disk_encryption
fields.doc: Whether to enable LUKS on cluster VMs' local disks

fields.name: executors

fields.name: gcp_attributes
fields.doc:
Attributes related to clusters running on Google Cloud Platform. If not
specified at cluster creation, a set of default values will be used.

fields.name: init_scripts
fields.doc:
The configuration for storing init scripts. Any number of destinations
can be specified. The scripts are executed sequentially in the order
provided. If `cluster_log_conf` is specified, init script logs are sent
to `<destination>/<cluster-ID>/init_scripts`.

fields.name: instance_pool_id
fields.doc: The optional ID of the instance pool to which the cluster belongs.

fields.name: is_single_node
fields.doc:
This field can only be used when `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.

When set to true, Databricks will automatically set single node related
`custom_tags`, `spark_conf`, and `num_workers`

fields.name: jdbc_port
fields.doc:
Port on which Spark JDBC server is listening, in the driver nod. No
service will be listeningon on this port in executor nodes.

fields.name: last_restarted_time

subset of the cluster tags

types.name: DataSecurityMode
types.doc:
Data security mode decides what data governance model to use when accessing
data from a cluster.

* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_AUTO`: Databricks will choose the most appropriate
access mode depending on your compute configuration. *
`DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`: A secure cluster that can be shared by
multiple users. Cluster users are fully isolated so that they cannot see each
other’s data and credentials. Most data governance features are supported
in this mode. But programming languages and cluster features might be
limited. * `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`: A secure cluster that can only be
exclusively used by a single user specified in `single_user_name`. Most
programming languages, cluster features and data governance features are
available in this mode.

The following modes are legacy aliases for the above modes:

* `USER_ISOLATION`: Legacy alias for `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`. *
`SINGLE_USER`: Legacy alias for `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`.

The following modes are deprecated starting with Databricks Runtime 15.0 and
will be removed for future Databricks Runtime versions:

* `LEGACY_TABLE_ACL`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Table ACL
clusters. * `LEGACY_PASSTHROUGH`: This mode is for users migrating from
legacy Passthrough on high concurrency clusters. * `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER`: This
mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on standard clusters. *
`LEGACY_SINGLE_USER_STANDARD`: This mode provides a way that doesn’t have
UC nor passthrough enabled.

values.doc:

compute configuration.

in `single_user_name`. Most programming languages, cluster features and data
governance features are available in this mode.

fully isolated so that they cannot see each other’s data and credentials.
Most data governance features are supported in this mode. But programming
languages and cluster features might be limited.

This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on high concurrency
clusters.

This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on standard
clusters.
This mode provides a way that doesn’t have UC nor passthrough enabled.
This mode is for users migrating from legacy Table ACL clusters.
Legacy alias for `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`.
Legacy alias for `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`.

* `DEPENDENCY_MODE_AUTO`: Databricks will choose the most appropriate

experience across classic and serverless, resulting in increased stability
and performance. Supported only on DBR 19+ in Standard access mode. *
`DEPENDENCY_MODE_CLUSTER_LIBRARIES`: Legacy mode: dependencies come from
cluster libraries and init scripts.
