Whether to enable PG native password login on the instance. Defaults to
false.

fields.name: enable_readable_secondaries
fields.doc:
Whether to enable secondaries to serve read-only traffic. Defaults to
false.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The name of the instance. This is the unique identifier for the instance.

fields.name: node_count
fields.doc:
The number of nodes in the instance, composed of 1 primary and 0 or more
secondaries. Defaults to 1 primary and 0 secondaries. This field is input
only, see effective_node_count for the output.

fields.name: parent_instance_ref
fields.doc:
The ref of the parent instance. This is only available if the instance is
child instance. Input: For specifying the parent instance to create a
child instance. Optional. Output: Only populated if provided as input to
create a child instance.

fields.name: pg_version
fields.doc: The version of Postgres running on the instance.

fields.name: read_only_dns
fields.doc:
The DNS endpoint to connect to the instance for read only access. This is
only available if enable_readable_secondaries is true.

fields.name: read_write_dns
fields.doc: The DNS endpoint to connect to the instance for read+write access.

fields.name: retention_window_in_days
fields.doc:
The retention window for the instance. This is the time window in days
for which the historical data is retained. The default value is 7 days.
Valid values are 2 to 35 days.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: The current state of the instance.

fields.name: stopped
fields.doc:
Whether to stop the instance. An input only param, see effective_stopped
for the output.

fields.name: uid
fields.doc: An immutable UUID identifier for the instance.

fields.name: usage_policy_id
fields.doc: The desired usage policy to associate with the instance.

types.name: DatabaseInstanceRef
types.doc:
DatabaseInstanceRef is a reference to a database instance. It is used in the
DatabaseInstance object to refer to the parent instance of an instance and to
refer the child instances of an instance. To specify as a parent instance
during creation of an instance, the lsn and branch_time fields are optional.
If not specified, the child instance will be created from the latest lsn of
the parent. If both lsn and branch_time are specified, the lsn will be used
to create the child instance.

fields.name: branch_time
fields.doc:
Branch time of the ref database instance. For a parent ref instance, this
is the point in time on the parent instance from which the instance was
created. For a child ref instance, this is the point in time on the
instance from which the child instance was created. Input: For specifying
the point in time to create a child instance. Optional. Output: Only
populated if provided as input to create a child instance.

fields.name: effective_lsn
fields.doc:
For a parent ref instance, this is the LSN on the parent instance from
which the instance was created. For a child ref instance, this is the LSN
on the instance from which the child instance was created. This is an
output only field that contains the value computed from the input field
combined with server side defaults. Use the field without the effective_
prefix to set the value.

fields.name: lsn
fields.doc:
User-specified WAL LSN of the ref database instance.

Input: For specifying the WAL LSN to create a child instance. Optional.
Output: Only populated if provided as input to create a child instance.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Name of the ref database instance.

fields.name: uid
fields.doc: Id of the ref database instance.

types.name: DatabaseInstanceRole
types.doc: A DatabaseInstanceRole represents a Postgres role in a database instance.

fields.name: attributes
fields.doc:
The desired API-exposed Postgres role attribute to associate with the
role. Optional.

fields.name: effective_attributes
fields.doc:
The attributes that are applied to the role. This is an output only field
that contains the value computed from the input field combined with
server side defaults. Use the field without the effective_ prefix to set
the value.

fields.name: identity_type
fields.doc: The type of the role.

fields.name: membership_role
fields.doc: An enum value for a standard role that this role is a member of.

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
The name of the role. This is the unique identifier for the role in an
instance.

types.name: DatabaseInstanceRoleAttributes
types.doc:
Attributes that can be granted to a Postgres role. We are only implementing a
subset for now, see xref:
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/sql-createrole.html The values follow
Postgres keyword naming e.g. CREATEDB, BYPASSRLS, etc. which is why they
don't include typical underscores between words. We were requested to make
this a nested object/struct representation since these are knobs from an
external spec.

types.name: DatabaseInstanceRoleMembershipRole
types.doc: Roles that the DatabaseInstanceRole can be a member of.

fields.name: database_instance_name
fields.doc:
Name of the target database instance. This is required when creating
database tables in standard catalogs. This is optional when creating
database tables in registered catalogs. If this field is specified when
creating database tables in registered catalogs, the database instance
name MUST match that of the registered catalog (or the request will be
rejected).

fields.name: logical_database_name
fields.doc:
Target Postgres database object (logical database) name for this table.

When creating a table in a standard catalog, this field is required. In
this scenario, specifying this field will allow targeting an arbitrary
postgres database.

Registration of database tables via /database/tables is currently only
supported in standard catalogs.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Full three-part (catalog, schema, table) name of the table.

fields.name: force
fields.doc:
By default, an instance cannot be deleted if it has descendant instances
created via PITR. If this flag is specified as true, all descendent
instances will be deleted as well.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Name of the instance to delete.

fields.name: purge
fields.doc:
Deprecated. Omitting the field or setting it to true will result in the
field being hard deleted. Setting a value of false will throw a bad
request.

fields.name: allow_missing
fields.doc:
This is the AIP standard name for the equivalent of Postgres' `IF EXISTS`
option

fields.name: purge_data
fields.doc:
Optional. When set to true, the actual PostgreSQL table will be dropped
from the database.

fields.name: delta_commit_timestamp
fields.doc:
The timestamp when the above Delta version was committed in the source
Delta table. Note: This is the Delta commit time, not the time the data
was written to the synced table.

fields.name: delta_commit_version
fields.doc: The Delta Lake commit version that was last successfully synced.

fields.name: uid
fields.doc: UID of the cluster to get.

types.name: GenerateDatabaseCredentialRequest
types.doc: Generates a credential that can be used to access database instances

fields.name: claims
fields.doc:
A set of UC permissions to add to the credential. We verify that the
caller has the necessary permissions in UC and include a reference in the
token. Postgres uses that token to give the connecting user additional
grants to the Postgres resources that correspond to the UC resources. The
UC resources need to be something that have a Postgres counterpart. For
example, a synced table or a table in a UC database catalog.

fields.name: instance_names
fields.doc:
Instances to request a credential for. At least one of instance_names or
claims must be specified.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Name of the cluster to get.

fields.name: instance_name
fields.doc: Name of the instance to get database catalogs for.

fields.name: page_size
fields.doc: Upper bound for items returned.

fields.name: page_token
fields.doc:
Pagination token to go to the next page of synced database tables.
Requests first page if absent.

fields.name: next_page_token
fields.doc: Pagination token to request the next page of database catalogs.

fields.name: page_size
fields.doc: Upper bound for items returned.

fields.name: page_token
fields.doc:
Pagination token to go to the next page of Database Instances. Requests
first page if absent.

fields.name: database_instance_roles
fields.doc: List of database instance roles.

fields.name: next_page_token
fields.doc: Pagination token to request the next page of instances.

fields.name: page_size
fields.doc: Upper bound for items returned. The maximum value is 100.

fields.name: page_token
fields.doc:
Pagination token to go to the next page of Database Instances. Requests
first page if absent.

fields.name: database_instances
fields.doc: List of instances.

fields.name: next_page_token
fields.doc: Pagination token to request the next page of instances.

fields.name: instance_name
fields.doc: Name of the instance to get synced tables for.

fields.name: page_size
fields.doc: Upper bound for items returned.

fields.name: page_token
fields.doc:
Pagination token to go to the next page of synced database tables.
Requests first page if absent.

fields.name: next_page_token
fields.doc: Pagination token to request the next page of synced tables.

types.name: NewPipelineSpec
types.doc:
Custom fields that user can set for pipeline while creating
SyncedDatabaseTable. Note that other fields of pipeline are still inferred by
table def internally

fields.name: budget_policy_id
fields.doc: Budget policy to set on the newly created pipeline.

fields.name: storage_catalog
fields.doc:
This field needs to be specified if the destination catalog is a managed
postgres catalog.

UC catalog for the pipeline to store intermediate files (checkpoints,
event logs etc). This needs to be a standard catalog where the user has
permissions to create Delta tables.

fields.name: storage_schema
fields.doc:
This field needs to be specified if the destination catalog is a managed
postgres catalog.

UC schema for the pipeline to store intermediate files (checkpoints,
event logs etc). This needs to be in the standard catalog where the user
has permissions to create Delta tables.

types.name: RequestedClaimsPermissionSet
types.doc: Might add WRITE in the future

fields.name: data_synchronization_status
fields.doc: Synced Table data synchronization status

fields.name: database_instance_name
fields.doc:
Name of the target database instance. This is required when creating
synced database tables in standard catalogs. This is optional when
creating synced database tables in registered catalogs. If this field is
specified when creating synced database tables in registered catalogs,
the database instance name MUST match that of the registered catalog (or
the request will be rejected).

fields.name: effective_database_instance_name
fields.doc:
The name of the database instance that this table is registered to. This
field is always returned, and for tables inside database catalogs is
inferred database instance associated with the catalog. This is an output
only field that contains the value computed from the input field combined
with server side defaults. Use the field without the effective_ prefix to
set the value.

fields.name: effective_logical_database_name
fields.doc:
The name of the logical database that this table is registered to. This
is an output only field that contains the value computed from the input
field combined with server side defaults. Use the field without the
effective_ prefix to set the value.

fields.name: logical_database_name
fields.doc:
Target Postgres database object (logical database) name for this table.

When creating a synced table in a registered Postgres catalog, the target
Postgres database name is inferred to be that of the registered catalog.
If this field is specified in this scenario, the Postgres database name
MUST match that of the registered catalog (or the request will be
rejected).

When creating a synced table in a standard catalog, this field is
required. In this scenario, specifying this field will allow targeting an
arbitrary postgres database. Note that this has implications for the
`create_database_objects_is_missing` field in `spec`.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Full three-part (catalog, schema, table) name of the table.

fields.name: unity_catalog_provisioning_state
fields.doc:
The provisioning state of the synced table entity in Unity Catalog. This
is distinct from the state of the data synchronization pipeline (i.e. the
table may be in "ACTIVE" but the pipeline may be in "PROVISIONING" as it
runs asynchronously).

types.name: SyncedTableContinuousUpdateStatus
types.doc:
Detailed status of a synced table. Shown if the synced table is in the
SYNCED_CONTINUOUS_UPDATE or the SYNCED_UPDATING_PIPELINE_RESOURCES state.

fields.name: initial_pipeline_sync_progress
fields.doc: Progress of the initial data synchronization.

fields.name: last_processed_commit_version
fields.doc:
The last source table Delta version that was successfully synced to the
synced table.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc:
The end timestamp of the last time any data was synchronized from the
source table to the synced table. This is when the data is available in
the synced table.

types.name: SyncedTableFailedStatus
types.doc:
Detailed status of a synced table. Shown if the synced table is in the
OFFLINE_FAILED or the SYNCED_PIPELINE_FAILED state.

fields.name: last_processed_commit_version
fields.doc:
The last source table Delta version that was successfully synced to the
synced table. The last source table Delta version that was synced to the
synced table. Only populated if the table is still synced and available
for serving.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc:
The end timestamp of the last time any data was synchronized from the
source table to the synced table. Only populated if the table is still
synced and available for serving.

types.name: SyncedTablePipelineProgress
types.doc: Progress information of the Synced Table data synchronization pipeline.

fields.name: estimated_completion_time_seconds
fields.doc: The estimated time remaining to complete this update in seconds.

fields.name: latest_version_currently_processing
fields.doc:
The source table Delta version that was last processed by the pipeline.
The pipeline may not have completely processed this version yet.

fields.name: provisioning_phase
fields.doc: The current phase of the data synchronization pipeline.

fields.name: sync_progress_completion
fields.doc: The completion ratio of this update. This is a number between 0 and 1.

fields.name: synced_row_count
fields.doc: The number of rows that have been synced in this update.

fields.name: total_row_count
fields.doc:
The total number of rows that need to be synced in this update. This
number may be an estimate.

fields.name: sync_end_timestamp
fields.doc:
The end timestamp of the most recent successful synchronization. This is
the time when the data is available in the synced table.

fields.name: sync_start_timestamp
fields.doc:
The starting timestamp of the most recent successful synchronization from
the source table to the destination (synced) table. Note this is the
starting timestamp of the sync operation, not the end time. E.g., for a
batch, this is the time when the sync operation started.

types.name: SyncedTableProvisioningStatus
types.doc:
Detailed status of a synced table. Shown if the synced table is in the
PROVISIONING_PIPELINE_RESOURCES or the PROVISIONING_INITIAL_SNAPSHOT state.

fields.name: initial_pipeline_sync_progress
fields.doc:
Details about initial data synchronization. Only populated when in the
PROVISIONING_INITIAL_SNAPSHOT state.

types.name: SyncedTableSpec
types.doc: Specification of a synced database table.

fields.name: accelerated_sync
fields.doc:
When true, enables accelerated sync mode for the initial data load. This
significantly improves performance for large tables. Requires
workspace-level enablement.

fields.name: create_database_objects_if_missing
fields.doc:
If true, the synced table's logical database and schema resources in PG
will be created if they do not already exist.

fields.name: existing_pipeline_id
fields.doc:
At most one of existing_pipeline_id and new_pipeline_spec should be
defined.

If existing_pipeline_id is defined, the synced table will be bin packed
into the existing pipeline referenced. This avoids creating a new
pipeline and allows sharing existing compute. In this case, the
scheduling_policy of this synced table must match the scheduling policy
of the existing pipeline.

fields.name: new_pipeline_spec
fields.doc:
At most one of existing_pipeline_id and new_pipeline_spec should be
defined.

If new_pipeline_spec is defined, a new pipeline is created for this
synced table. The location pointed to is used to store intermediate files
(checkpoints, event logs etc). The caller must have write permissions to
create Delta tables in the specified catalog and schema. Again, note this
requires write permissions, whereas the source table only requires read
permissions.

fields.name: primary_key_columns
fields.doc: Primary Key columns to be used for data insert/update in the destination.

fields.name: scheduling_policy
fields.doc: Scheduling policy of the underlying pipeline.

fields.name: source_table_full_name
fields.doc: Three-part (catalog, schema, table) name of the source Delta table.

fields.name: timeseries_key
fields.doc:
Time series key to deduplicate (tie-break) rows with the same primary
key.

fields.name: type_overrides
fields.doc:
Override the default Delta->PG type mapping for specific columns. A
TypeOverride with PG_SPECIFIC_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED is rejected; a valid
pg_type must be set.

types.name: SyncedTableSpecPgSpecificType
types.doc:
PostgreSQL-specific target types that can override the default Delta-to-PG
mapping.

types.name: SyncedTableSpecTypeOverride
types.doc: Overrides the default Delta-to-PostgreSQL type mapping for a single column.

fields.name: column_name
fields.doc:
Name of the source column whose target PostgreSQL type should be
overridden.

fields.name: pg_type
fields.doc: PostgreSQL-specific target type to use for the column.

fields.name: size
fields.doc:
Size parameter for the target type, for types that take one (e.g. vector
dimension, varchar length). Required when the chosen pg_type needs a
size.

types.name: SyncedTableState
types.doc: The state of a synced table.

types.name: SyncedTableStatus
types.doc: Status of a synced table.

fields.name: detailed_state
fields.doc: The state of the synced table.

fields.name: last_sync
fields.doc:
Summary of the last successful synchronization from source to
destination.

Will always be present if there has been a successful sync. Even if the
most recent syncs have failed.

Limitation: The only exception is if the synced table is doing a FULL
REFRESH, then the last sync information will not be available until the
full refresh is complete. This limitation will be addressed in a future
version.

This top-level field is a convenience for consumers who want easy access
to last sync information without having to traverse detailed_status.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: A text description of the current state of the synced table.

fields.name: pipeline_id
fields.doc:
ID of the associated pipeline. The pipeline ID may have been provided by
the client (in the case of bin packing), or generated by the server (when
creating a new pipeline).

types.name: SyncedTableTriggeredUpdateStatus
types.doc:
Detailed status of a synced table. Shown if the synced table is in the
SYNCED_TRIGGERED_UPDATE or the SYNCED_NO_PENDING_UPDATE state.

fields.name: last_processed_commit_version
fields.doc:
The last source table Delta version that was successfully synced to the
synced table.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc:
The end timestamp of the last time any data was synchronized from the
source table to the synced table. This is when the data is available in
the synced table.

fields.name: triggered_update_progress
fields.doc: Progress of the active data synchronization pipeline.

fields.name: database_catalog
fields.doc: Note that updating a database catalog is not yet supported.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The name of the catalog in UC.

fields.name: update_mask
fields.doc: The list of fields to update. Setting this field is not yet supported.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The name of the instance. This is the unique identifier for the instance.

fields.name: update_mask
fields.doc:
The list of fields to update. If unspecified, all fields will be updated
when possible. To wipe out custom_tags, specify custom_tags in the
update_mask with an empty custom_tags map.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Full three-part (catalog, schema, table) name of the table.

fields.name: synced_table
fields.doc: Note that updating a synced database table is not yet supported.

fields.name: update_mask
fields.doc: The list of fields to update. Setting this field is not yet supported.

types.name: AutoTaggingConfig
types.doc:
Auto-tagging configuration for a classification tag. When enabled, detected
columns are automatically tagged with Unity Catalog tags.

fields.name: auto_tagging_mode
fields.doc: Whether auto-tagging is enabled or disabled for this classification tag.

fields.name: classification_tag
fields.doc:
The Classification Tag. For built-in classes this is a system tag (e.g.,
"class.name", "class.location"); for custom classes it is a user-defined
governance tag key.

types.name: AutoTaggingConfigAutoTaggingMode
types.doc: Auto-tagging mode.

types.name: CatalogConfig
types.doc:
Data Classification configuration for a Unity Catalog catalog. This message
follows the "At Most One Resource" pattern: at most one CatalogConfig exists
per catalog. - Full CRUD operations are supported: Create enables Data
Classification, Delete disables it - It has no unique identifier of its own
and uses its parent catalog's identifier (catalog_name)

fields.name: auto_tag_configs
fields.doc:
List of auto-tagging configurations for this catalog. Empty list means no
auto-tagging is enabled.

fields.name: excluded_schemas
fields.doc:
Schemas to exclude from the scan, each named relative to the parent
catalog. If specified, all schemas except the specified ones will be
scanned. Mutually exclusive with `included_schemas`: only one may be set
per request. If neither `included_schemas` nor `excluded_schemas` is set,
all schemas are scanned.

fields.name: included_schemas
fields.doc:
Schemas to include in the scan, each named relative to the parent
catalog. If specified, only listed schemas will be scanned. Mutually
exclusive with `excluded_schemas`: only one may be set per request. If
neither `included_schemas` nor `excluded_schemas` is set, all schemas are
scanned.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Resource name in the format: catalogs/{catalog_name}/config.

types.name: CatalogConfigSchemaNames
types.doc: Wrapper message for a list of schema names.

fields.name: names
fields.doc: Schema names, each relative to the parent catalog. Must not be empty.

fields.name: catalog_config
fields.doc: The configuration to create.

fields.name: parent
fields.doc: Parent resource in the format: catalogs/{catalog_name}

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Resource name in the format: catalogs/{catalog_name}/config

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Resource name in the format: catalogs/{catalog_name}/config

fields.name: catalog_config
fields.doc:
The configuration to apply to the catalog. The name field in
catalog_config identifies which resource to update.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Resource name in the format: catalogs/{catalog_name}/config.

fields.name: update_mask
fields.doc: Field mask specifying which fields to update.

types.name: AggregationGranularity
types.doc:
The granularity for aggregating data into time windows based on their
timestamp.

types.name: AnomalyDetectionConfig
types.doc: Anomaly Detection Configurations.

fields.name: excluded_table_full_names
fields.doc: List of fully qualified table names to exclude from anomaly detection.

types.name: CancelRefreshRequest
types.doc: Request to cancel a refresh.

fields.name: object_id
fields.doc:
The UUID of the request object. It is `schema_id` for `schema`, and
`table_id` for `table`.

Find the `schema_id` from either: 1. The [schema_id] of the `Schemas`
resource. 2. In [Catalog Explorer] > select the `schema` > go to the
`Details` tab > the `Schema ID` field.

Find the `table_id` from either: 1. The [table_id] of the `Tables`
resource. 2. In [Catalog Explorer] > select the `table` > go to the
`Details` tab > the `Table ID` field.

[Catalog Explorer]: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/catalog-explorer/
[schema_id]: https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/schemas/get#schema_id
[table_id]: https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/tables/get#table_id

fields.name: object_type
fields.doc:
The type of the monitored object. Can be one of the following: `schema`
or `table`.

fields.name: refresh_id
fields.doc: Unique id of the refresh operation.

types.name: CancelRefreshResponse
types.doc: Response to cancelling a refresh.

fields.name: refresh
fields.doc: The refresh to cancel.

fields.name: monitor
fields.doc: The monitor to create.

fields.name: object_id
fields.doc:
The UUID of the request object. It is `schema_id` for `schema`, and
`table_id` for `table`.

Find the `schema_id` from either: 1. The [schema_id] of the `Schemas`
resource. 2. In [Catalog Explorer] > select the `schema` > go to the
`Details` tab > the `Schema ID` field.

Find the `table_id` from either: 1. The [table_id] of the `Tables`
resource. 2. In [Catalog Explorer] > select the `table` > go to the
`Details` tab > the `Table ID` field.

[Catalog Explorer]: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/catalog-explorer/
[schema_id]: https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/schemas/get#schema_id
[table_id]: https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/tables/get#table_id

fields.name: object_type
fields.doc:
The type of the monitored object. Can be one of the following: `schema`
or `table`.

fields.name: refresh
fields.doc: The refresh to create

types.name: CronSchedule
types.doc: The data quality monitoring workflow cron schedule.

fields.name: pause_status
fields.doc: Read only field that indicates whether the schedule is paused or not.

fields.name: quartz_cron_expression
fields.doc:
The expression that determines when to run the monitor. See [examples].

[examples]: https://www.quartz-scheduler.org/documentation/quartz-2.3.0/tutorials/crontrigger.html

fields.name: timezone_id
fields.doc:
A Java timezone id. The schedule for a job will be resolved with respect
to this timezone. See `Java TimeZone
<http://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/util/TimeZone.html>`_ for
details. The timezone id (e.g., ``America/Los_Angeles``) in which to
evaluate the quartz expression.

types.name: CronSchedulePauseStatus
types.doc: The data quality monitoring workflow cron schedule pause status.

types.name: DataProfilingConfig
types.doc: Data Profiling Configurations.

fields.name: assets_dir
fields.doc:
Field for specifying the absolute path to a custom directory to store
data-monitoring assets. Normally prepopulated to a default user location
via UI and Python APIs.

fields.name: baseline_table_name
fields.doc:
Baseline table name. Baseline data is used to compute drift from the data
in the monitored `table_name`. The baseline table and the monitored table
shall have the same schema.

fields.name: custom_metrics
fields.doc: Custom metrics.

fields.name: dashboard_id
fields.doc:
Id of dashboard that visualizes the computed metrics. This can be empty
if the monitor is in PENDING state.

fields.name: drift_metrics_table_name
fields.doc:
Table that stores drift metrics data. Format:
`catalog.schema.table_name`.

fields.name: effective_warehouse_id
fields.doc: The warehouse for dashboard creation

fields.name: inference_log
fields.doc: `Analysis Configuration` for monitoring inference log tables.

fields.name: latest_monitor_failure_message
fields.doc: The latest error message for a monitor failure.

fields.name: monitor_version
fields.doc:
Represents the current monitor configuration version in use. The version
will be represented in a numeric fashion (1,2,3...). The field has
flexibility to take on negative values, which can indicate corrupted
monitor_version numbers.

fields.name: monitored_table_name
fields.doc: Unity Catalog table to monitor. Format: `catalog.schema.table_name`

fields.name: notification_settings
fields.doc: Field for specifying notification settings.

fields.name: output_schema_id
fields.doc: ID of the schema where output tables are created.

fields.name: profile_metrics_table_name
fields.doc:
Table that stores profile metrics data. Format:
`catalog.schema.table_name`.

fields.name: schedule
fields.doc: The cron schedule.

fields.name: skip_builtin_dashboard
fields.doc:
Whether to skip creating a default dashboard summarizing data quality
metrics.

fields.name: slicing_exprs
fields.doc:
List of column expressions to slice data with for targeted analysis. The
data is grouped by each expression independently, resulting in a separate
slice for each predicate and its complements. For example
`slicing_exprs=[“col_1”, “col_2 > 10”]` will generate the
following slices: two slices for `col_2 > 10` (True and False), and one
slice per unique value in `col1`. For high-cardinality columns, only the
top 100 unique values by frequency will generate slices.

fields.doc:
Etag used for versioning. The response is at least as fresh as the eTag
provided. Etag is used for optimistic concurrency control as a way to
help prevent simultaneous updates of a rule set from overwriting each
other. It is strongly suggested that systems make use of the etag in the
read -> modify -> write pattern to perform rule set updates in order to
avoid race conditions that is get an etag from a GET rule set request,
and pass it with the PUT update request to identify the rule set version
you are updating.

Examples | Summary :--- | :--- `etag=` | An empty etag can only be used
in GET to indicate no freshness requirements.
`etag=RENUAAABhSweA4NvVmmUYdiU717H3Tgy0UJdor3gE4a+mq/oj9NjAf8ZsQ==` | An
etag encoded a specific version of the rule set to get or to be updated.

Identifies the version of the rule set returned. Etag used for
versioning. The response is at least as fresh as the eTag provided. Etag
is used for optimistic concurrency control as a way to help prevent
simultaneous updates of a rule set from overwriting each other. It is
strongly suggested that systems make use of the etag in the read ->
modify -> write pattern to perform rule set updates in order to avoid
race conditions that is get an etag from a GET rule set request, and pass
it with the PUT update request to identify the rule set version you are
updating.

types.name: WorkspaceAssignment
types.doc:
The direct assignment of a provisioned account-level principal (user, service
principal, or group) to a workspace, together with the entitlements that
assignment grants in the workspace.

This resource covers only principals assigned directly to the workspace.
Principals that inherit workspace access through a group are not represented
here. See WorkspaceAccessDetail and WorkspaceIdentityDetail for the
effective, direct-or-indirect view. Creating the resource assigns the
principal to the workspace, and deleting it removes the assignment.

`entitlements` is the only client-settable field. It holds the entitlements
granted directly on this assignment, including any the principal also holds
through a group. `effective_entitlements` is the read-only union of those and
any granted through group membership.

A direct assignment always carries at least one directly-assigned
entitlement, because the assignment is what grants it. Create and update both
reject an empty `entitlements` set. To remove a principal's assignment
entirely, delete the resource.

This resource replaces workspace assignment previously managed through the
workspace SCIM and permission-assignment APIs, and is intended for account
and workspace admins.

fields.name: account_id
fields.doc: The account ID parent of the workspace where the principal is assigned

fields.name: effective_entitlements

Every entitlement the principal holds in this workspace, whether granted

List responses leave it empty.

fields.name: entitlements
fields.doc:
Entitlements granted directly to the principal on this workspace. This is
the only client-settable field. Create and update manage exactly this
set, including entitlements the principal also holds through a group.
List responses leave this field empty. Get a single principal to read its
entitlements.

The type of the principal (user/service principal/group) that is

types.name: AiRuntimeTask
types.doc:
AiRuntimeTask: multi-node GPU compute task definition for Databricks AI
Runtime workloads.

Jobs-framework-level concepts (retries, per-task timeout, idempotency token,
usage/budget policy, permissions) live on the surrounding TaskSettings /
run-submit request and are intentionally NOT duplicated here. Users compose
`ai_runtime_task` with the standard Jobs/DABs task wrapper to get those.

fields.name: code_source_path
fields.doc:
Workspace or UC volume path of the code-source archive, unpacked on each
node and exposed through `$CODE_SOURCE`. Set by first-party tooling; not
for direct callers.

fields.name: deployments
fields.doc:
Deployment specs for this task. Exactly one deployment is currently
supported (a single entry where every node runs the same command); this
is a current-Preview constraint. Role-split workloads (driver + worker,
parameter server, separate eval node, etc.) with multiple entries are the
eventual intent but not yet supported.

fields.name: docker_image_url
fields.doc:
Optional Docker image URL for a custom container image. When set, the
task runs on the specified container image instead of the default
Databricks client image. Format: `{organization}/{repository}:{tag}`

fields.name: experiment
fields.doc:
MLflow experiment name for this run. If an experiment with this name
already exists under the calling user, the run is appended to it;
otherwise a new experiment is created. To target a specific MLflow
storage location (for example, when running as a service principal), set
`mlflow_experiment_directory`.

fields.name: mlflow_artifact_location
fields.doc:
Optional root location for MLflow artifacts logged by the run. If this
field isn't specified the default artifact location will be in dbfs i.e.
`dbfs:/databricks/mlflow-tracking/<experiment_id>/...` If dbfs access is
restricted or UC is preferred this can be a custom location in UC:
`dbfs:/Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>/...` The location should be
unique for each experiment.

fields.name: mlflow_experiment_directory
fields.doc:
Optional workspace directory under which the MLflow experiment named in
`experiment` is created. Must start with `/Workspace`. Set this when
running as a service principal that has no default user directory; for
regular users the experiment defaults to the user's home directory.

fields.name: mlflow_run
fields.doc:
Optional display name for the MLflow run created under `experiment`. If
omitted, MLflow generates a default name.

fields.name: priority_class
fields.doc:
Scheduling priority class for the workload. May only be set together with
a pre-provisioned capacity reservation (a deployment's
`compute.provisioned_capacity_id`); it is rejected on a workload that
runs on on-demand capacity.

fields.name: unity_catalog_image_path
fields.doc:
Optional Unity Catalog path for a custom container image. When set, the
task runs on the specified container image instead of the default
Databricks client image. Format: `{catalog}.{schema}.{image_name}:{tag}`

types.name: AiRuntimeTaskOutput
types.doc:
AiRuntimeTaskOutput: output identifiers for an AiRuntimeTask run — the
MLflow experiment and run IDs the task wrote to.

Run lifecycle and termination status are not on this message; they live on
the surrounding `RunTask.status` field (see `runs.proto:RunTask.status`).

fields.name: mlflow_experiment_id
fields.doc:
MLflow experiment ID the run was logged to. Use it to look up the
experiment in MLflow APIs or the workspace MLflow UI.

fields.name: mlflow_run_id
fields.doc:
MLflow run ID for this task execution. Use it to look up the run in
MLflow APIs or the workspace MLflow UI.

fields.name: status_message
fields.doc:
Human-readable status message for this run, suitable for display to the
user (for example, that the run is still waiting for GPU compute). Set by
the server only when there is something to surface; empty otherwise.

types.name: AiRuntimeTaskPriorityClass
types.doc:
Scheduling priority class for a workload — its priority and preemptability
when the scheduler ranks pending work.

types.name: AlertEvaluationState
types.doc: Same alert evaluation state as in redash-v2/api/proto/alertsv2/alerts.proto

fields.name: alert_id
fields.doc: The alert_id is the canonical identifier of the alert.

fields.name: parameters
fields.doc:
Per-run parameter overrides, keyed by parameter name, applied onto the
alert's stored query parameters before the query is executed. Only scalar
values are supported. Values may reference job parameters with
`{{job.parameters.*}}`, which are resolved before the task runs. An
override whose key does not match a stored parameter fails the task run.
Limited to 10000 characters when serialized as JSON; keys must be 1-100
characters and contain only letters, digits, underscores, dashes, and
periods.

fields.name: subscribers
fields.doc:
The subscribers receive alert evaluation result notifications after the
alert task is completed. The number of subscriptions is limited to 100.

fields.name: warehouse_id
fields.doc:
The warehouse_id identifies the warehouse settings used by the alert
task.

fields.name: workspace_path
fields.doc:
The workspace_path is the path to the alert file in the workspace. The
path: * must start with "/Workspace" * must be a normalized path. User
has to select only one of alert_id or workspace_path to identify the
alert.

types.name: AlertTaskSubscriber
types.doc:
Represents a subscriber that will receive alert notifications. A subscriber
can be either a user (via email) or a notification destination (via
destination_id).

fields.name: user_name
fields.doc: A valid workspace email address.

fields.name: created_time
fields.doc:
The time at which this job was created in epoch milliseconds
(milliseconds since 1/1/1970 UTC).

fields.name: creator_user_name
fields.doc:
The creator user name. This field won’t be included in the response if
the user has already been deleted.

fields.name: effective_budget_policy_id
fields.doc:
The id of the budget policy used by this job for cost attribution
purposes. This may be set through (in order of precedence): 1. Budget
admins through the account or workspace console 2. Jobs UI in the job
details page and Jobs API using `budget_policy_id` 3. Inferred default
based on accessible budget policies of the run_as identity on job
creation or modification.

fields.name: effective_usage_policy_id
fields.doc:
The id of the usage policy used by this job for cost attribution
purposes.

fields.name: has_more
fields.doc:
Indicates if the job has more array properties (`tasks`, `job_clusters`)
that are not shown. They can be accessed via :method:jobs/get endpoint.
It is only relevant for API 2.2 :method:jobs/list requests with
`expand_tasks=true`.

fields.name: job_id
fields.doc: The canonical identifier for this job.

fields.name: settings
fields.doc:
Settings for this job and all of its runs. These settings can be updated
using the `resetJob` method.

fields.name: trigger_details
fields.doc:
Per-trigger runtime information for the multi-trigger surface. Same
length and order as `JobSettings.triggers`; `trigger_details[i]`
corresponds to `triggers[i]`. Sub-fields (`state`, `history`) are
populated independently based on the `GetJob.include_trigger_state` /
`include_trigger_history` flags.

fields.name: trigger_state
fields.doc: State of the trigger associated with the job.

fields.name: attempt_number
fields.doc:
The sequence number of this run attempt for a triggered job run. The
initial attempt of a run has an attempt_number of 0. If the initial run
attempt fails, and the job has a retry policy (`max_retries` > 0),
subsequent runs are created with an `original_attempt_run_id` of the
original attempt’s ID and an incrementing `attempt_number`. Runs are
retried only until they succeed, and the maximum `attempt_number` is the
same as the `max_retries` value for the job.

fields.name: cleanup_duration
fields.doc:
The time in milliseconds it took to terminate the cluster and clean up
any associated artifacts. The duration of a task run is the sum of the
`setup_duration`, `execution_duration`, and the `cleanup_duration`. The
`cleanup_duration` field is set to 0 for multitask job runs. The total
duration of a multitask job run is the value of the `run_duration` field.

fields.name: cluster_instance
fields.doc:
The cluster used for this run. If the run is specified to use a new
cluster, this field is set once the Jobs service has requested a cluster
for the run.

fields.name: cluster_spec
fields.doc:
A snapshot of the job’s cluster specification when this run was
created.

fields.name: creator_user_name
fields.doc:
The creator user name. This field won’t be included in the response if
the user has already been deleted.

fields.name: deployment_id
fields.doc:
ID of the deployment that produced the job when this run was created.
Used to look up deployment metadata from the Deployment Metadata service.
Only set for job runs of jobs with a `BUNDLE` deployment.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: Description of the run

fields.name: effective_performance_target
fields.doc:
The actual performance target used by the serverless run during
execution. This can differ from the client-set performance target on the
request depending on whether the performance mode is supported by the job
type.

* `PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZED`: Prioritizes fast startup and execution times
through rapid scaling and optimized cluster performance. * `STANDARD`:
Enables cost-efficient execution of serverless workloads. *
`COST_OPTIMIZED`: Enables lower job costs by optimizing compute for your
selected target duration time. Must provide a duration target.

fields.name: effective_usage_policy_id
fields.doc:
The id of the usage policy used by this run for cost attribution
purposes.

fields.name: end_time
fields.doc:
The time at which this run ended in epoch milliseconds (milliseconds
since 1/1/1970 UTC). This field is set to 0 if the job is still running.

fields.name: execution_duration
fields.doc:
The time in milliseconds it took to execute the commands in the JAR or
notebook until they completed, failed, timed out, were cancelled, or
encountered an unexpected error. The duration of a task run is the sum of
the `setup_duration`, `execution_duration`, and the `cleanup_duration`.
The `execution_duration` field is set to 0 for multitask job runs. The
total duration of a multitask job run is the value of the `run_duration`
field.

fields.name: git_source
fields.doc:
An optional specification for a remote Git repository containing the
source code used by tasks. Version-controlled source code is supported by
notebook, dbt, Python script, and SQL File tasks.

If `git_source` is set, these tasks retrieve the file from the remote
repository by default. However, this behavior can be overridden by
setting `source` to `WORKSPACE` on the task.

Note: dbt and SQL File tasks support only version-controlled sources. If
dbt or SQL File tasks are used, `git_source` must be defined on the job.

fields.name: has_more
fields.doc:
Indicates if the run has more array properties (`tasks`, `job_clusters`)
that are not shown. They can be accessed via :method:jobs/getrun
endpoint. It is only relevant for API 2.2 :method:jobs/listruns requests
with `expand_tasks=true`.

fields.name: job_clusters
fields.doc:
A list of job cluster specifications that can be shared and reused by
tasks of this job. Libraries cannot be declared in a shared job cluster.
You must declare dependent libraries in task settings. If more than 100
job clusters are available, you can paginate through them using
:method:jobs/getrun.

fields.name: job_id
fields.doc: The canonical identifier of the job that contains this run.

fields.name: job_parameters
fields.doc: Job-level parameters used in the run

fields.name: job_run_id
fields.doc:
ID of the job run that this run belongs to. For legacy and single-task
job runs the field is populated with the job run ID. For task runs, the
field is populated with the ID of the job run that the task run belongs
to.

fields.name: number_in_job
fields.doc:
A unique identifier for this job run. This is set to the same value as
`run_id`.

fields.name: original_attempt_run_id
fields.doc:
If this run is a retry of a prior run attempt, this field contains the
run_id of the original attempt; otherwise, it is the same as the run_id.

fields.name: overriding_parameters
fields.doc: The parameters used for this run.

fields.name: queue_duration
fields.doc: The time in milliseconds that the run has spent in the queue.

fields.name: repair_history
fields.doc: The repair history of the run.

fields.name: run_duration
fields.doc:
The time in milliseconds it took the job run and all of its repairs to
finish.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc:
The canonical identifier of the run. This ID is unique across all runs of
all jobs.

fields.name: run_name
fields.doc:
An optional name for the run. The maximum length is 4096 bytes in UTF-8
encoding.

fields.name: run_page_url
fields.doc: The URL to the detail page of the run.

fields.name: schedule
fields.doc:
The cron schedule that triggered this run if it was triggered by the
periodic scheduler.

fields.name: setup_duration
fields.doc:
The time in milliseconds it took to set up the cluster. For runs that run
on new clusters this is the cluster creation time, for runs that run on
existing clusters this time should be very short. The duration of a task
run is the sum of the `setup_duration`, `execution_duration`, and the
`cleanup_duration`. The `setup_duration` field is set to 0 for multitask
job runs. The total duration of a multitask job run is the value of the
`run_duration` field.

fields.name: start_time
fields.doc:
The time at which this run was started in epoch milliseconds
(milliseconds since 1/1/1970 UTC). This may not be the time when the job
task starts executing, for example, if the job is scheduled to run on a
new cluster, this is the time the cluster creation call is issued.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Deprecated. Please use the `status` field instead.

fields.name: tasks
fields.doc:
The list of tasks performed by the run. Each task has its own `run_id`
which you can use to call `JobsGetOutput` to retrieve the run results. If
more than 100 tasks are available, you can paginate through them using
:method:jobs/getrun. Use the `next_page_token` field at the object root
to determine if more results are available.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc:
ID of the deployment version that produced the job when this run was
created. Identifies a specific snapshot of the deployment in the
Deployment Metadata service. Only set for job runs of jobs with a
`BUNDLE` deployment.

fields.name: all_queued_runs
fields.doc:
Optional boolean parameter to cancel all queued runs. If no job_id is
provided, all queued runs in the workspace are canceled.

fields.name: job_id
fields.doc: The canonical identifier of the job to cancel all runs of.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: This field is required.

types.name: CleanRoomTaskRunLifeCycleState
types.doc:
Copied from elastic-spark-common/api/messages/runs.proto. Using the original
definition to remove coupling with jobs API definition

types.name: CleanRoomTaskRunResultState
types.doc:
Copied from elastic-spark-common/api/messages/runs.proto. Using the original
definition to avoid cyclic dependency.

types.name: CleanRoomTaskRunState
types.doc: Stores the run state of the clean rooms notebook task.

fields.name: life_cycle_state
fields.doc:
A value indicating the run's current lifecycle state. This field is
always available in the response. Note: Additional states might be
introduced in future releases.

fields.name: result_state
fields.doc:
A value indicating the run's result. This field is only available for
terminal lifecycle states. Note: Additional states might be introduced in
future releases.

types.name: CleanRoomsNotebookTask
types.doc:
Clean Rooms notebook task for V1 Clean Room service (GA). Replaces the
deprecated CleanRoomNotebookTask (defined above) which was for V0 service.

fields.name: clean_room_name
fields.doc: The clean room that the notebook belongs to.

fields.name: etag
fields.doc:
Checksum to validate the freshness of the notebook resource (i.e. the
notebook being run is the latest version). It can be fetched by calling
the :method:cleanroomassets/get API.

fields.name: notebook_base_parameters
fields.doc: Base parameters to be used for the clean room notebook job.

fields.name: notebook_name
fields.doc: Name of the notebook being run.

fields.name: clean_room_job_run_state
fields.doc: The run state of the clean rooms notebook task.

fields.name: notebook_output
fields.doc: The notebook output for the clean room run

fields.name: output_schema_info
fields.doc: Information on how to access the output schema for the clean room run

fields.name: cluster_id
fields.doc:
The canonical identifier for the cluster used by a run. This field is
always available for runs on existing clusters. For runs on new clusters,
it becomes available once the cluster is created. This value can be used
to view logs by browsing to `/#setting/sparkui/$cluster_id/driver-logs`.
The logs continue to be available after the run completes.

The response won’t include this field if the identifier is not
available yet.

fields.name: spark_context_id
fields.doc:
The canonical identifier for the Spark context used by a run. This field
is filled in once the run begins execution. This value can be used to
view the Spark UI by browsing to
`/#setting/sparkui/$cluster_id/$spark_context_id`. The Spark UI continues
to be available after the run has completed.

The response won’t include this field if the identifier is not
available yet.

fields.name: existing_cluster_id
fields.doc:
If existing_cluster_id, the ID of an existing cluster that is used for
all runs. When running jobs or tasks on an existing cluster, you may need
to manually restart the cluster if it stops responding. We suggest
running jobs and tasks on new clusters for greater reliability

fields.name: job_cluster_key
fields.doc:
If job_cluster_key, this task is executed reusing the cluster specified
in `job.settings.job_clusters`.

fields.name: libraries
fields.doc:
An optional list of libraries to be installed on the cluster. The default
value is an empty list.

fields.name: new_cluster
fields.doc:
If new_cluster, a description of a new cluster that is created for each
run.

fields.name: hardware_accelerator
fields.doc: Hardware accelerator configuration for Serverless GPU workloads.

fields.name: gpu_node_pool_id
fields.doc: IDof the GPU pool to use.

fields.name: gpu_type
fields.doc: GPU type.

fields.name: num_gpus
fields.doc: Number of GPUs.

types.name: ComputeSpec
types.doc:
ComputeSpec: compute configuration — accelerator type and total accelerator
count across all nodes.

fields.name: accelerator_count
fields.doc:
Total number of accelerators across all nodes. Must be a positive
multiple of the per-node accelerator count encoded in `accelerator_type`.
For example, `GPU_8xH100` with `accelerator_count: 16` allocates 2 nodes
(8 GPUs per node).

fields.name: accelerator_type
fields.doc:
Hardware accelerator type (for example, `GPU_1xA10` or `GPU_8xH100`). The
number of accelerators per node is encoded in the enum value —
`GPU_8xH100` means 8 H100 GPUs per node.

fields.name: provisioned_capacity_id
fields.doc:
Optional ID of a pre-provisioned accelerator capacity reservation to run
this AI Runtime workload on. When set, the workload is scheduled onto the
referenced reserved capacity instead of the on-demand capacity shared
among all Databricks customers.

types.name: ComputeSpecAcceleratorType
types.doc:
Hardware accelerator type for the AiRuntime workload. Per-node accelerator
count is encoded in the value name (e.g. `GPU_8xH100` means 8 H100s per
node).

fields.name: left
fields.doc:
The left operand of the condition task. Can be either a string value or a
job state or parameter reference.

fields.name: op
fields.doc:
* `EQUAL_TO`, `NOT_EQUAL` operators perform string comparison of their
operands. This means that `“12.0” == “12”` will evaluate to
`false`. * `GREATER_THAN`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL`, `LESS_THAN`,
`LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL` operators perform numeric comparison of their
operands. `“12.0” >= “12”` will evaluate to `true`, `“10.0”
>= “12”` will evaluate to `false`.

The boolean comparison to task values can be implemented with operators
`EQUAL_TO`, `NOT_EQUAL`. If a task value was set to a boolean value, it
will be serialized to `“true”` or `“false”` for the comparison.

fields.name: right
fields.doc:
The right operand of the condition task. Can be either a string value or
a job state or parameter reference.

types.name: ConditionTaskOp
types.doc:
* `EQUAL_TO`, `NOT_EQUAL` operators perform string comparison of their
operands. This means that `“12.0” == “12”` will evaluate to `false`.
* `GREATER_THAN`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL`, `LESS_THAN`, `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL`
operators perform numeric comparison of their operands. `“12.0” >=
“12”` will evaluate to `true`, `“10.0” >= “12”` will evaluate to
`false`.

The boolean comparison to task values can be implemented with operators
`EQUAL_TO`, `NOT_EQUAL`. If a task value was set to a boolean value, it will
be serialized to `“true”` or `“false”` for the comparison.

fields.name: maintenance_window
fields.doc:
Defines when platform-initiated maintenance may run for this job. If
unspecified, maintenance may run at any time.

fields.name: pause_status
fields.doc:
Indicate whether the continuous execution of the job is paused or not.
Defaults to UNPAUSED.

fields.name: task_retry_mode
fields.doc:
Indicate whether the continuous job is applying task level retries or
not. Defaults to NEVER.

types.name: ContinuousTriggerConfiguration
types.doc:
Continuous trigger. Stripped-down counterpart to `ContinuousSettings`:
`pause_status` is owned by the enclosing `TriggerConfiguration` and
intentionally omitted here.

fields.name: maintenance_window
fields.doc:
Defines when platform-initiated maintenance may run for this trigger. If
unspecified, maintenance may run at any time.

fields.name: task_retry_mode
fields.doc: Whether the continuous job applies task-level retries. Defaults to NEVER.

fields.name: access_control_list
fields.doc: List of permissions to set on the job.

fields.name: budget_policy_id
fields.doc:
The id of the user specified budget policy to use for this job. If not
specified, a default budget policy may be applied when creating or
modifying the job. See `effective_budget_policy_id` for the budget policy
used by this workload.

fields.name: continuous
fields.doc:
An optional continuous property for this job. The continuous property
will ensure that there is always one run executing. Only one of
`schedule` and `continuous` can be used.

Pipelines started by a continuous job also run continuously, regardless
of their own pipeline mode setting.

fields.name: deployment
fields.doc: Deployment information for jobs managed by external sources.

fields.name: description
fields.doc:
An optional description for the job. The maximum length is 27700
characters in UTF-8 encoding.

fields.name: edit_mode
fields.doc:
Edit mode of the job.

* `UI_LOCKED`: The job is in a locked UI state and cannot be modified. *
`EDITABLE`: The job is in an editable state and can be modified.

fields.name: email_notifications
fields.doc:
An optional set of email addresses that is notified when runs of this job
begin or complete as well as when this job is deleted.

fields.name: environments
fields.doc:
A list of task execution environment specifications that can be
referenced by tasks that use serverless compute or a compute resource
that uses Environments mode.

For notebook tasks that use serverless compute or a compute resource that
uses Environments mode, if the environment_key is not specified, the
notebook environment will be used if present. If a jobs environment is
specified, it will override the notebook environment. For other tasks
that use serverless compute or a compute resource that uses Environments
mode, the task environment is required to be specified using
environment_key in the task settings.

fields.name: format
fields.doc:
Used to tell what is the format of the job. This field is ignored in
Create/Update/Reset calls. When using the Jobs API 2.1 this value is
always set to `"MULTI_TASK"`.

fields.name: git_source
fields.doc:
An optional specification for a remote Git repository containing the
source code used by tasks. Version-controlled source code is supported by
notebook, dbt, Python script, and SQL File tasks.

If `git_source` is set, these tasks retrieve the file from the remote
repository by default. However, this behavior can be overridden by
setting `source` to `WORKSPACE` on the task.

Note: dbt and SQL File tasks support only version-controlled sources. If
dbt or SQL File tasks are used, `git_source` must be defined on the job.

fields.name: job_clusters
fields.doc:
A list of job cluster specifications that can be shared and reused by
tasks of this job. Libraries cannot be declared in a shared job cluster.
You must declare dependent libraries in task settings.

fields.name: max_concurrent_runs
fields.doc:
An optional maximum allowed number of concurrent runs of the job. Set
this value if you want to be able to execute multiple runs of the same
job concurrently. This is useful for example if you trigger your job on a
frequent schedule and want to allow consecutive runs to overlap with each
other, or if you want to trigger multiple runs which differ by their
input parameters. This setting affects only new runs. For example,
suppose the job’s concurrency is 4 and there are 4 concurrent active
runs. Then setting the concurrency to 3 won’t kill any of the active
runs. However, from then on, new runs are skipped unless there are fewer
than 3 active runs. This value cannot exceed 1000. Setting this value to
`0` causes all new runs to be skipped.

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
An optional name for the job. The maximum length is 4096 bytes in UTF-8
encoding.

fields.name: notification_settings
fields.doc:
Optional notification settings that are used when sending notifications
to each of the `email_notifications` and `webhook_notifications` for this
job.

fields.name: parameters
fields.doc: Job-level parameter definitions

fields.name: parent_path
fields.doc:
Path of the job parent folder in workspace file tree. If absent, the job
doesn't have a workspace object.

fields.name: performance_target
fields.doc:
The performance mode on a serverless job. This field determines the level
of compute performance or cost-efficiency for the run. The performance
target does not apply to tasks that run on Serverless GPU compute.

* `PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZED`: Prioritizes fast startup and execution times
through rapid scaling and optimized cluster performance. * `STANDARD`:
Enables cost-efficient execution of serverless workloads. *
`COST_OPTIMIZED`: Enables lower job costs by optimizing compute for your
selected target duration time. Must provide a duration target.

fields.name: queue
fields.doc: The queue settings of the job.

fields.name: run_as
fields.doc:
The user or service principal that the job runs as, if specified in the
request. This field indicates the explicit configuration of `run_as` for
the job. To find the value in all cases, explicit or implicit, use
`run_as_user_name`.

fields.name: schedule
fields.doc:
An optional periodic schedule for this job. The default behavior is that
the job only runs when triggered by clicking “Run Now” in the Jobs UI
or sending an API request to `runNow`.

fields.name: tags
fields.doc:
A map of tags associated with the job. These are forwarded to the cluster
as cluster tags for jobs clusters, and are subject to the same
limitations as cluster tags. A maximum of 25 tags can be added to the
job.

fields.name: tasks
fields.doc:
A list of task specifications to be executed by this job. It supports up
to 1000 elements in write endpoints (:method:jobs/create,
:method:jobs/reset, :method:jobs/update, :method:jobs/submit). Read
endpoints return only 100 tasks. If more than 100 tasks are available,
you can paginate through them using :method:jobs/get. Use the
`next_page_token` field at the object root to determine if more results
are available.

fields.name: timeout_seconds
fields.doc:
An optional timeout applied to each run of this job. A value of `0` means
no timeout.

fields.name: trigger
fields.doc:
A configuration to trigger a run when certain conditions are met. The
default behavior is that the job runs only when triggered by clicking
“Run Now” in the Jobs UI or sending an API request to `runNow`.

fields.name: triggers
fields.doc:
List of triggers attached to this job. A run starts when any active
trigger evaluates to true. Cannot be set in the same request as the
legacy `schedule`, `trigger`, or `continuous` fields. Gated behind the
"Multiple Triggers" feature preview.

fields.name: usage_policy_id
fields.doc:
The id of the user specified usage policy to use for this job. If not
specified, a default usage policy may be applied when creating or
modifying the job. See `effective_usage_policy_id` for the usage policy
used by this workload.

fields.name: webhook_notifications
fields.doc:
A collection of system notification IDs to notify when runs of this job
begin or complete.

types.name: CreateResponse
types.doc: Job was created successfully

fields.name: job_id
fields.doc: The canonical identifier for the newly created job.

fields.name: pause_status
fields.doc: Indicate whether this schedule is paused or not.

fields.name: quartz_cron_expression
fields.doc:
A Cron expression using Quartz syntax that describes the schedule for a
job. See [Cron Trigger] for details. This field is required.

[Cron Trigger]: http://www.quartz-scheduler.org/documentation/quartz-2.3.0/tutorials/crontrigger.html

fields.name: sql_condition
fields.doc:
SQL condition that must be satisfied before a scheduled run is triggered.
The condition is evaluated after the cron expression fires and must
return a truthy result for the run to proceed.

fields.name: timezone_id
fields.doc:
A Java timezone ID. The schedule for a job is resolved with respect to
this timezone. See [Java TimeZone] for details. This field is required.

[Java TimeZone]: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/util/TimeZone.html

types.name: CronTriggerConfiguration
types.doc:
Cron schedule trigger. Stripped-down counterpart to `CronSchedule`:
`pause_status` and `sql_condition` are owned by the enclosing
`TriggerConfiguration` and intentionally omitted here.

fields.name: quartz_cron_expression
fields.doc:
A Cron expression using Quartz syntax that describes the schedule for
this trigger. See [Cron Trigger] for details.

[Cron Trigger]: http://www.quartz-scheduler.org/documentation/quartz-2.3.0/tutorials/crontrigger.html

fields.name: timezone_id
fields.doc:
A Java timezone ID. The schedule is resolved with respect to this
timezone. See [Java TimeZone] for details.

[Java TimeZone]: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/util/TimeZone.html

types.name: DashboardTask
types.doc: Configures the Lakeview Dashboard job task type.

fields.name: dashboard_id
fields.doc: The identifier of the dashboard to refresh.

fields.name: filters
fields.doc:
Dashboard task parameters. Used to apply dashboard filter values during
dashboard task execution. Parameter values get applied to any dashboard
filters that have a matching URL identifier as the parameter key. The
parameter value format is dependent on the filter type: - For text and
single-select filters, provide a single value (e.g. `"value"`) - For date
and datetime filters, provide the value in ISO 8601 format (e.g.
`"2000-01-01T00:00:00"`) - For multi-select filters, provide a JSON array
of values (e.g. `"[\"value1\",\"value2\"]"`) - For range and date range
filters, provide a JSON object with `start` and `end` (e.g.
`"{\"start\":\"1\",\"end\":\"10\"}"`)

Whether the number of steps in the output has been truncated. If true,
the output will contain the first 20 steps of the output.

fields.name: catalog
fields.doc:
Optional name of the catalog to use. The value is the top level in the
3-level namespace of Unity Catalog (catalog / schema / relation). The
catalog value can only be specified if a warehouse_id is specified.
Requires dbt-databricks >= 1.1.1.

fields.name: commands
fields.doc:
A list of dbt commands to execute. All commands must start with `dbt`.
This parameter must not be empty. A maximum of up to 10 commands can be
provided.

fields.name: profiles_directory
fields.doc:
Optional (relative) path to the profiles directory. Can only be specified
if no warehouse_id is specified. If no warehouse_id is specified and this
folder is unset, the root directory is used.

fields.name: project_directory
fields.doc:
Path to the project directory. Optional for Git sourced tasks, in which
case if no value is provided, the root of the Git repository is used.

fields.name: schema
fields.doc:
Optional schema to write to. This parameter is only used when a
warehouse_id is also provided. If not provided, the `default` schema is
used.

fields.name: source
fields.doc:
Optional location type of the project directory. When set to `WORKSPACE`,
the project will be retrieved from the local Databricks workspace. When
set to `GIT`, the project will be retrieved from a Git repository defined
in `git_source`. If the value is empty, the task will use `GIT` if
`git_source` is defined and `WORKSPACE` otherwise.

* `WORKSPACE`: Project is located in Databricks workspace. * `GIT`:
Project is located in cloud Git provider.

fields.name: warehouse_id
fields.doc:
ID of the SQL warehouse to connect to. If provided, we automatically
generate and provide the profile and connection details to dbt. It can be
overridden on a per-command basis by using the `--profiles-dir` command
line argument.

fields.name: job_id
fields.doc: The canonical identifier of the job to delete. This field is required.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: ID of the run to delete.

types.name: DeploymentSpec
types.doc:
DeploymentSpec: configuration for one deployment within an AiRuntimeTask.
Each entry in `AiRuntimeTask.deployments` describes a group of nodes that
share the same command and compute. Many single-program training algorithms
use a single entry where every node runs the same command; role-split
workloads (driver + worker, parameter server, separate eval node, etc.) use
multiple entries.

fields.name: command_path
fields.doc:
Workspace path of the script to run on each node in this deployment.
Upload the script to this path and supply the path here. When the task
runs, the file at this path is run on each node; if it fails, the task
fails with its exit code.

Example script contents:

# Plain Python: python train.py --epochs 10

# Multi-GPU via accelerate: accelerate launch train.py --config
config.yaml

# Distributed via torchrun: torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 train.py

fields.name: compute
fields.doc: Compute resources allocated to each node in this deployment.

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
Optional human-readable name for this deployment (for example, `driver`,
`worker`, `param_server`). Used for log and UI display. Distinct names
are recommended so deployments can be told apart, but uniqueness is not
enforced.

types.name: EnforcePolicyComplianceForJobResponseJobClusterSettingsChange
types.doc:
Represents a change to the job cluster's settings that would be required for
the job clusters to become compliant with their policies.

fields.name: field
fields.doc:
The field where this change would be made, prepended with the job cluster
key.

fields.name: new_value
fields.doc:
The new value of this field after enforcing policy compliance (either a
number, a boolean, or a string) converted to a string. This is intended
to be read by a human. The typed new value of this field can be retrieved
by reading the settings field in the API response.

fields.name: previous_value
fields.doc:
The previous value of this field before enforcing policy compliance
(either a number, a boolean, or a string) converted to a string. This is
intended to be read by a human. The type of the field can be retrieved by
reading the settings field in the API response.

fields.name: job_id
fields.doc: The ID of the job you want to enforce policy compliance on.

fields.name: validate_only
fields.doc:
If set, previews changes made to the job to comply with its policy, but
does not update the job.

fields.name: has_changes
fields.doc:
Whether any changes have been made to the job cluster settings for the
job to become compliant with its policies.

fields.name: job_cluster_changes
fields.doc:
A list of job cluster changes that have been made to the job’s cluster
settings in order for all job clusters to become compliant with their
policies.

fields.name: settings
fields.doc:
Updated job settings after policy enforcement. Policy enforcement only
applies to job clusters that are created when running the job (which are
specified in new_cluster) and does not apply to existing all-purpose
clusters. Updated job settings are derived by applying policy default
values to the existing job clusters in order to satisfy policy
requirements.

types.name: ExportRunOutput
types.doc: Run was exported successfully.

fields.name: views
fields.doc:
The exported content in HTML format (one for every view item). To extract
the HTML notebook from the JSON response, download and run this [Python
script](/_static/examples/extract.py).

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: The canonical identifier for the run. This field is required.

fields.name: views_to_export
fields.doc: Which views to export (CODE, DASHBOARDS, or ALL). Defaults to CODE.

fields.name: min_time_between_triggers_seconds
fields.doc:
If set, the trigger starts a run only after the specified amount of time
passed since the last time the trigger fired. The minimum allowed value
is 60 seconds

fields.name: url
fields.doc:
URL to be monitored for file arrivals. The path must point to the root or
a subpath of the external location.

fields.name: wait_after_last_change_seconds
fields.doc:
If set, the trigger starts a run only after no file activity has occurred
for the specified amount of time. This makes it possible to wait for a
batch of incoming files to arrive before triggering a run. The minimum
allowed value is 60 seconds.

fields.name: using_file_events
fields.doc:
Indicates whether the trigger leverages file events to detect file
arrivals.

fields.name: error_message_stats
fields.doc: Sample of 3 most common error messages occurred during the iteration.

fields.name: task_run_stats
fields.doc: Describes stats of the iteration. Only latest retries are considered.

fields.name: concurrency
fields.doc:
An optional maximum allowed number of concurrent runs of the task. Set
this value if you want to be able to execute multiple runs of the task
concurrently.

fields.name: inputs
fields.doc:
Array for task to iterate on. This can be a JSON string or a reference to
an array parameter.

fields.name: task
fields.doc: Configuration for the task that will be run for each element in the array

fields.name: count
fields.doc:
Describes the count of such error message encountered during the
iterations.

fields.name: error_message
fields.doc: Describes the error message occurred during the iterations.

fields.name: termination_category
fields.doc: Describes the termination reason for the error message.

fields.name: active_iterations
fields.doc:
Describes the iteration runs having an active lifecycle state or an
active run sub state.

fields.name: completed_iterations
fields.doc: Describes the number of failed and succeeded iteration runs.

fields.name: failed_iterations
fields.doc: Describes the number of failed iteration runs.

fields.name: scheduled_iterations
fields.doc: Describes the number of iteration runs that have been scheduled.

fields.name: succeeded_iterations
fields.doc: Describes the number of succeeded iteration runs.

fields.name: total_iterations
fields.doc: Describes the length of the list of items to iterate over.

types.doc:
DEPRECATED — use `AiRuntimeTask` for all new BYOT multi-node GPU workloads
(see ai_runtime_task.proto). `AiRuntimeTask` is the only supported BYOT task
type for new workloads; this proto is retained only for AIR CLI (fka SGCLI)
pywheel backwards compatibility and will be removed once the pywheel →

fields.name: command

fields.name: dl_runtime_image

fields.name: mlflow_experiment_name
fields.doc:
Optional string containing the name of the MLflow experiment to log the
run to. If name is not found, backend will create the mlflow experiment
using the name.

fields.name: source
fields.doc:
Optional location type of the training script. When set to `WORKSPACE`,
the script will be retrieved from the local Databricks workspace. When
set to `GIT`, the script will be retrieved from a Git repository defined
in `git_source`. If the value is empty, the task will use `GIT` if
`git_source` is defined and `WORKSPACE` otherwise. * `WORKSPACE`: Script
is located in Databricks workspace. * `GIT`: Script is located in cloud
Git provider.

fields.name: training_script_path
fields.doc:
The training script file path to be executed. Cloud file URIs (such as
dbfs:/, s3:/, adls:/, gcs:/) and workspace paths are supported. For
python files stored in the Databricks workspace, the path must be
absolute and begin with `/`. For files stored in a remote repository, the
path must be relative. This field is required.

fields.name: yaml_parameters
fields.doc:
Optional string containing model parameters passed to the training script
in yaml format. If present, then the content in yaml_parameters_file_path
will be ignored.

fields.name: yaml_parameters_file_path
fields.doc:
Optional path to a YAML file containing model parameters passed to the
training script.

Flag that indicates that trigger state should be included in the
response.

The canonical identifier of the job to retrieve information about. This
field is required.

fields.name: page_token

Use `next_page_token` returned from the previous GetJob response to

fields.name: job_id

fields.name: is_compliant
fields.doc:
Whether the job is compliant with its policies or not. Jobs could be out
of compliance if a policy they are using was updated after the job was
last edited and some of its job clusters no longer comply with their
updated policies.

fields.name: violations
fields.doc:
An object containing key-value mappings representing the first 200 policy
validation errors. The keys indicate the path where the policy validation
error is occurring. An identifier for the job cluster is prepended to the
path. The values indicate an error message describing the policy
validation error.

fields.name: run_id

fields.name: include_history
fields.doc: Whether to include the repair history in the response.

fields.name: include_resolved_values
